• Purity test: a pure solid melts sharply at one temperature; impurities LOWER the melting point and WIDEN the range. Pure liquids boil constantly.
  • Choosing separation: filtration (insoluble solid from liquid), crystallisation (heat-sensitive dissolved solid — slow cooling gives big crystals), evaporation (salt from brine), simple distillation (solvent from solution, e.g. seawater → water), fractional distillation (miscible liquids by b.p. — crude oil, ethanol–water), separating funnel (immiscible liquids), chromatography (dyes/amino acids).
  • Chromatography: Rf = distance of spot ÷ distance of solvent front (always ≤ 1, measured from baseline pencil line — never ink). Identical Rf in same solvent ⇒ possibly same substance.
  • Titration apparatus discipline: rinse burette with the solution it will hold, pipette with the solution it measures, conical flask with distilled water only. Read burette to 0.05 cm³ at eye level (meniscus). Indicators: methyl orange or phenolphthalein for strong acid–alkali.

• Core conversions: n = m/M · n = c × V(dm³) · n = V(gas)/24 dm³ at r.t.p. · N = n × 6.02 × 10²³.
  • Reacting masses: write the equation → moles of known → use the mole ratio → convert to the wanted quantity. This 4-step chain answers EVERY mass/mass, mass/volume and titration question.
  • % yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100. Yield is lost by: incomplete reaction, side reactions, transfer losses, purification losses.
  • % purity = mass of pure substance ÷ mass of impure sample × 100.
  • Empirical formula: % ÷ Ar → ÷ smallest → whole numbers (multiply ×2 if .5 appears). Molecular formula = (empirical)ₙ where n = M ÷ empirical mass.
  • Concentration conversions: mol/dm³ = g/dm³ ÷ M. Dilutions: c₁V₁ = c₂V₂.

• Proton number = electrons (neutral atom); nucleon number = p + n. Isotopes = same protons, different neutrons: ¹²C (standard), ¹⁴C (carbon dating), ²H (heavy hydrogen), ²³⁵U (fuel).
  • Ionic bonding: electron TRANSFER metal→non-metal; giant lattice; conducts when molten/aqueous (mobile ions); high m.p.; brittle (like ions repel when layers shift).
  • Covalent: SHARING. Simple molecular (H₂O, CO₂, I₂): low m.p., non-conductors, often soluble in organic solvents. Giant covalent (diamond: 4 bonds, hardest, non-conductor; graphite: 3 bonds + delocalised electrons → conducts, slippery, used in electrodes/pencils; SiO₂ similar to diamond).
  • Metallic: cations in a sea of delocalised electrons → conducts, malleable (layers slide without breaking — electrons glue them).
  • Dot-and-cross diagrams REQUIRED for NaCl, MgO, CaCl₂, H₂, H₂O, CO₂, CH₄, NH₃.

• OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons). Oxidising agent accepts electrons (is itself reduced).
  • Electrolytes: molten/aqueous ionic compounds, acids, alkalis — NOT sugar, ethanol, pure water (very weak).
  • Discharge rules: cation of a metal BELOW H in the reactivity series is discharged; H⁺ is discharged from aqueous solutions of metals ABOVE H. Anions: halide discharged (except very dilute solutions → O₂), otherwise OH⁻ → O₂, SO₄²⁻/NO₃⁻ never discharged.
  • Brine (conc. NaCl): cathode H₂, anode Cl₂, solution becomes NaOH — the chlor-alkali industry.
  • Active electrodes: Cu anode dissolves (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻); used in electroplating (spoon as cathode) and copper refining.
  • Quantitative: moles of e⁻ = Q ÷ 96 500 C; e.g. Cu²⁺ needs 2e⁻ per atom.

• Exothermic (ΔH negative, heat released): combustion, neutralisation, respiration, freezing, condensation. Endothermic: thermal decomposition (CaCO₃), photosynthesis, dissolving NH₄Cl, melting, boiling.
  • Energy profile diagrams: reactants→peak = activation energy Ea; difference reactants→products = ΔH. Label BOTH arrows.
  • Bond energy estimate: ΔH = Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed). Breaking = endothermic, making = exothermic.
  • Calorimetry: q = mcΔθ; assume 1 cm³ water = 1 g, c = 4.18 J/g°C; heat loss → measured ΔH smaller in magnitude than true value.
  • Fuel choices compare: energy per gram, availability, pollution, storage.

• Collision theory: reaction needs collisions with energy ≥ Ea and correct orientation.
  • Factors: concentration/pressure (more particles per volume → more frequent collisions), surface area (powder ≫ lumps), temperature (T +10°C ≈ doubles rate — more collisions AND more exceed Ea), catalyst (alternative route, LOWER Ea; unchanged chemically at the end; enzymes are biological catalysts).
  • Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution: catalyst does NOT shift the curve or increase temperature — it lowers the Ea line, so more particles qualify.
  • Graphs: gradient = rate; steepest at start (reactants most concentrated); curves level off when a reactant finishes. SAME final volume with/without catalyst — catalyst only changes SPEED.
  • Measuring rate: gas syringe volume vs time, mass loss (CO₂ escapes), cross-disappearance (sulfur precipitate), titrating samples vs time.

• Acid = H⁺ donor; alkali = soluble base (OH⁻ in water). pH < 7 acid, > 7 alkali; universal indicator colour scale; strong (HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃) fully ionise; weak (ethanoic, carbonic) partially.
  • Reactions: acid + metal → salt + H₂ · acid + carbonate → salt + H₂O + CO₂ · acid + alkali → salt + H₂O (neutralisation) · acid + oxide/hydroxide → salt + water.
  • Soluble salt preparation: (a) titration for Na⁺/K⁺/NH₄⁺ salts (exact quantities, indicator removed by evaporation to near-dryness before adding salt-forming acid); (b) add EXCESS insoluble reactant to acid, filter excess, crystallise filtrate.
  • Insoluble salts: precipitation — mix two soluble salts containing the wanted ions, filter, wash with distilled water, dry (e.g. BaSO₄, AgCl, PbSO₄, CaCO₃).
  • Tests: NH₄⁺ (warm with NaOH → NH₃ turns damp red litmus blue) · Fe²⁺ dirty-green ppt / Fe³⁺ reddish-brown / Cu²⁺ pale-blue with NaOH(aq) · Cl⁻ white ppt with AgNO₃/HNO₃ · SO₄²⁻ white ppt with BaCl₂/HCl · CO₃²⁻ effervescence with acid (CO₂ → limewater milky).

• Group I (alkali metals): soft, shiny→tarnish instantly, float, melt more easily down the group, react with water → hydroxide + H₂; reactivity INCREASES down (outer electron further from nucleus, more shielding → lost more easily).
  • Group VII (halogens): coloured (F₂ pale yellow, Cl₂ green, Br₂ red-brown, I₂ grey-black), diatomic, reactivity DECREASES down (harder to gain an electron). Displacement: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂ (a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its salt).
  • Group 0 (noble gases): full outer shell → unreactive; uses: Ar (welding, bulbs), Ne (advertising signs), He (balloons, diving gas, coolant), Kr/Xe (lamps, lasers).
  • Transition metals (between II and III): high m.p., hard, variable oxidation states (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cu⁺/Cu²⁺), COLOURED compounds (Cu²⁺ blue, Fe²⁺ green, Fe³⁺ yellow-brown), catalysts (Fe — Haber; Ni — hydrogenation; V₂O₅ — Contact; Pt — car exhaust), form complex ions.

• Reactivity series: K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb (H) Cu Ag Au. Position decides: reaction with water/steam/dilute acid, displacement, extraction method.
  • Extraction: K–Al: electrolysis of molten ores (huge energy); Zn–Fe: reduction with carbon/carbon monoxide in a blast furnace; below Fe: roasting in air suffices.
  • Blast furnace: C + O₂ → CO₂; CO₂ + C → 2CO; Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂; limestone decomposes → CaO + CO₂; CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ slag (floats on iron, protects it; used for roads). Iron from the furnace = pig iron (brittle, 4% C) → steels by removing carbon and adding alloying metals.
  • Steel types: mild steel (buildings, cars — cheap, strong), stainless steel (Cr + Ni: cutlery, surgical tools — rustproof), high-carbon steel (drills, hammers — hard but brittle).
  • Rusting needs BOTH water and oxygen. Prevention: paint, oil/grease, plastic coating, galvanising (zinc coating — sacrificial even when scratched), sacrificial blocks (Mg/Zn on ships/pipelines), tin-plating (NOT sacrificial — if scratched, iron rusts faster).
  • Alloys: brass (Cu+Zn), bronze (Cu+Sn), solder (Pb+Sn, low m.p.), duralumin (Al alloy, aircraft — light + strong).

• Air composition (~vol): N₂ 78%, O₂ 21%, Ar 0.9%, CO₂ 0.04% (rising). Separated by fractional distillation of liquefied air.
  • Combustion of fuels: complete (plenty of O₂) → CO₂ + H₂O; incomplete (limited O₂) → CO (toxic, odourless, binds haemoglobin) or soot C.
  • Water treatment: screening → coagulation/flocculation (alum) → sedimentation → sand filtration → chlorination (kills microbes; debate: residual protection vs by-products). Fluoridation where practised.
  • Hard water contains Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺: temporary hardness = hydrogencarbonates (removed by BOILING → CaCO₃ precipitate), permanent = sulfates/chlorides (removed by ion-exchange or washing soda Na₂CO₃, not boiling). Hardness: wastes soap (scum), BUT Ca²⁺ reduces heart disease, tastes better, no lead dissolution from pipes.
  • Test for water: anhydrous CuSO₄ white → blue, or anhydrous CoCl₂ blue → pink.
  • Sulfur: mined by Frasch process; S + O₂ → SO₂ (pungent, acid rain precursor); Contact process: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅ catalyst, 450°C, ~2 atm) → oleum → H₂SO₄. Uses: fertilisers, batteries, detergents, paints.
  • Acid rain (SO₂, NOₓ from burning fossil fuels): pH < 5.6, corrodes limestone/iron, kills fish, leaches soil nutrients. Remedies: scrubbers, catalytic converters, cleaner fuels.

• Homologous series = same general formula, similar chemistry, gradual physical trend, successive members differ by CH₂ (14 u). Functional group = atom/group deciding chemistry.
  • Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (saturated, single bonds): generally unreactive except BURNING (CO₂ + H₂O) and SUBSTITUTION with Cl₂/Br₂ in sunlight (free-radical chain). Methane from anaerobic decay (biogas, landfill); alkanes from crude oil (fractional distillation) and cracking.
  • Cracking: big alkane → smaller alkane + ALKENE (+ H₂ sometimes); conditions: 400–700°C, alumina/silica catalyst. Why crack: petrol demand > supply of light fractions; alkenes are valuable feedstock.
  • Alkenes CₙH₂ₙ (one C=C): made by cracking; TEST = decolourise bromine water (orange→colourless) / acidified KMnO₄ (purple→colourless). Addition reactions: +H₂ (Ni catalyst → alkane), +steam (H₃PO₄ catalyst → alcohol), +HX, +X₂.
  • Polymerisation: n CH₂=CH₂ → poly(ethene) — addition polymer; repeat unit drawn with continuation bonds through brackets.

• Alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH: ethanol by FERMENTATION of sugars (yeast enzymes ~30°C, anaerobic, then fractional distillation) or hydration of ethene. Alcohols burn, react with Na (→H₂), oxidise on standing with air/bacteria → acids.
  • Carboxylic acids CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH: weak acids (partial ionisation, pH 3–5, still fizz with carbonates — slower than mineral acids). Ethanoic acid from oxidation of ethanol (vinegar).
  • Esters RCOOR′: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water (conc. H₂SO₄ catalyst); sweet/fruity smell; uses: perfumes, flavourings, solvents (ethyl ethanoate), fats/oils are esters of glycerol.
  • Saponification: fat/oil + NaOH → soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) + glycerol. Soapless detergents from petroleum sulfonates.
  • Isomerism: same molecular formula, different structure — draw chain, position and functional-group isomers from C₄ upwards.
  • Identification flow: bromine water (unsaturation), Na₂CO₃ (acid: effervesces), ester smell test, burning characteristics.

• Reversible reactions: ⇌, products can convert back. Dynamic equilibrium (closed container): forward rate = backward rate, concentrations constant.
  • Le Chatelier: change concentration/pressure/temperature → system shifts to COUNTERACT. Pressure: shifts to side with FEWER gas molecules. Temperature: raise T → shifts in ENDOTHERMIC direction. Catalyst: NO shift — reaches equilibrium FASTER.
  • Haber process N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH = −92 kJ/mol): Fe catalyst, ~450°C, ~200 atm. Compromise conditions: low T favours yield but is slow; high P favours yield but is expensive/dangerous.
  • Contact process 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃: V₂O₅ catalyst, 450°C, ~2 atm.
  • Fertilisers: N (ammonium salts, urea — from Haber NH₃), P (from phosphate rock + H₂SO₄), K (potassium chloride/sulfate). Excess fertiliser → eutrophication: algal bloom → decomposition depletes O₂ → aquatic death.
  • Green chemistry ideas: atom economy, catalysts replacing stoichiometric reagents, renewable feedstocks, non-toxic solvents.

olevel/phys5054.b:
• Base quantities & SI units: length m, mass kg, time s, current A, temperature K. Prefixes: n µ m c k M G.
  • Scalar (magnitude only): speed, distance, mass, energy, temperature. Vector (magnitude + direction): displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, weight.
  • Add vectors by scale drawing (parallelogram/tip-to-tail) or components: vₓ = v cos θ, v_y = v sin θ. A 30 N horizontal + 40 N vertical force = 50 N resultant (3-4-5 triangle).
  • Measuring instruments: metre rule (1 mm), micrometer screw gauge (0.01 mm — rotate ratchet 3 clicks), vernier calipers (0.1 mm). Zero error correction: subtract the zero reading.
  • Precaution culture: repeat readings → mean; avoid parallax (eye perpendicular to scale); for oscillations, time 20 swings and divide (reaction-time error ÷20).

• Speed = distance/time (scalar); velocity = displacement/time (vector). Acceleration = Δv/Δt, units m/s².
  • Distance–time graph: gradient = speed; curved = changing speed; horizontal = stationary. Speed–time graph: gradient = acceleration; AREA under graph = distance travelled; below-axis area = reverse travel.
  • SUVAT (constant acceleration ONLY): v = u + at · s = ut + ½at² · v² = u² + 2as · s = ½(u+v)t. Free fall: a = g = 9.8–10 m/s² downward, u may be 0.
  • Worked pattern: list u, v, a, s, t with signs (up = +) → choose the equation containing the unknown and knowns → solve → sanity-check the sign.
  • Terminal velocity: falling object accelerates until drag = weight (net force 0) → constant velocity; depends on shape/area (parachute), occurs quickly for low mass:area (raindrop).
  • Projectile motion: horizontal velocity CONSTANT; vertical velocity changes with g — solve the two directions independently.

• 1st law (inertia): constant velocity (or rest) unless a resultant force acts. Mass = inertia measure.
  • 2nd law: F = ma (resultant force); weight W = mg. 1 N = force giving 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².
  • 3rd law: action–reaction pairs are EQUAL, OPPOSITE, and act on DIFFERENT bodies (swimmer pushes water back — water pushes swimmer forward; rocket pushes gas down — gas pushes rocket up).
  • Everyday applications: seatbelts/airbags (increase stopping time → reduce force, F = Δp/Δt), crumple zones, head restraints.
  • Momentum p = mv (kg·m/s), vector. Conservation: total momentum before = after collision/explosion (no external resultant force). Elastic: KE also conserved; inelastic: KE lost to heat/sound/deformation.
  • Impulse = FΔt = Δp — cricket fielder draws hands back, egg-catching foam, high-jump landing mats: all lengthen Δt to reduce F.

• Moment of force = force × perpendicular distance from pivot (N·m). Principle of moments (equilibrium): sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments.
  • Centre of gravity: point where weight appears to act; find by plumb-line method for irregular lamina. Stable equilibrium: CG rises on tilting and falls back (wide base, low CG); unstable: CG falls away.
  • Conditions for equilibrium: ΣF = 0 AND Σmoments = 0.
  • Friction: useful (walking, braking, grip) & wasteful (overcome by lubricants, rollers, streamlining). Limiting friction vs kinetic friction.
  • Pressure = F/A (Pa). Increase A → decrease pressure (snowshoes, tractor tyres, drawing pins the other way). Hydraulic systems: P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ → force multiplication (car brakes, jacks) with incompressible liquid.
  • Hooke's law: extension ∝ load up to the limit of proportionality: F = kx. Beyond elastic limit → permanent deformation; breaking point next. Energy stored = ½Fx = area under F–x graph.

• Work = force × distance moved in force direction (J); W = Fs; work against friction → heat.
  • Energy forms: KE = ½mv², GPE = mgh, elastic, thermal, chemical, nuclear, electrical, sound, light. Conservation: transforms, never created/destroyed.
  • Power = work/time = energy/time (W); P = Fv for vehicles. Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input × 100%.
  • Energy resources: renewable (solar, wind, hydro, tidal, geothermal, biomass) vs non-renewable (fossil, nuclear). Compare by cost, reliability, pollution, location, startup cost. Solar cell → electricity directly; solar panel → heat water; wind → kinetic → electrical.
  • Degraded energy: every conversion loses some to heat — why efficiency < 100% always.

• States & particle model: solid (fixed positions, vibrate), liquid (slide past), gas (free, fast). Changes: melting, boiling/evaporation, condensation, sublimation (camphor, CO₂), deposition.
  • Evaporation vs boiling: evaporation below b.p., only surface, any temperature, cooling effect (fastest molecules escape → average KE falls); boiling at b.p., throughout liquid, constant T.
  • Specific heat capacity: E = mcΔθ. Water's huge c (4200 J/kg°C) → coolant, climate moderation. Experiment: heater method E = VIt, with insulation + lid + stir + repeat.
  • Latent heat: E = ml (fusion ~334 kJ/kg water; vaporisation ~2260 kJ/kg — large → steam burns worse than boiling water). Temperature constant during change of state — energy breaks/makes bonds not speed.
  • Conduction: metals — free electrons + lattice vibrations; convection — fluids only, by density differences; radiation — infrared EM waves, no medium, dull black surfaces best emitters/absorbers (vacuum flask: silvered walls, vacuum, insulating support, stopper).
  • Thermal expansion: gaps in bridges/railway tracks, bimetallic strips (thermostats); water anomaly: ice floats (4°C densest) — aquatic life survives winter.

• Wave = energy transfer without net matter movement. Transverse (light, ripples, EM): oscillation ⊥ travel. Longitudinal (sound, compression in springs): oscillation ∥ travel.
  • v = fλ; f = 1/T. Sound: ~330–340 m/s in air, faster in water/solids; needs a medium — NOT in vacuum. Light: 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum.
  • Reflection: angle i = angle r; plane mirrors → virtual/same size/same distance behind. Refraction: speed change → bending; into denser → towards normal; n = sin i/sin r; apparent depth < real depth.
  • Diffraction: spreading through gaps/obstacles — greatest when gap ≈ λ. Long waves (radio) diffract around hills; why you hear round corners.
  • Sound: compression/rarefaction; pitch ∝ frequency; loudness ∝ amplitude; quality ∝ waveform. Ultrasound > 20 kHz: sonar, fetal scanning, cleaning. Echo: distance = v × t/2.
  • EM spectrum order: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma. Uses & dangers of each band.

• Thin-lens ray rules: parallel ray → through far focus; focal ray → emerges parallel; central ray → straight. Real images: inverted, projectable; virtual: upright, cannot.
  • Camera: real, inverted, diminished between F and 2F. Magnifying glass: object inside F → virtual, upright, enlarged. Projector: object between F and 2F → real, inverted, enlarged beyond 2F.
  • Total internal reflection: light inside denser medium beyond the critical angle reflects totally: sin c = 1/n. Applications: optical fibres (endoscopy, broadband), periscopes, prisms in binoculars, sparkling diamonds.
  • Colours: white light disperses through a prism (red deviated least, violet most). Primary colours of light: red + green + blue = white.
  • Light travels in straight lines (pinhole camera; shadows; eclipses); speed 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum.

• Q = It (coulombs = amps × seconds). Conventional current + to −; electrons flow the other way.
  • EMF = total energy per coulomb from the source; p.d. = energy per coulomb across a component; both in volts. V = IR (Ohm's law — ohmic conductors only).
  • Series: same current; V splits; R_total = R₁+R₂+… Parallel: same V; current splits; 1/R = Σ1/Rᵢ. Household circuits are PARALLEL (each appliance full mains V; switches on live wire; fuses in live wire).
  • Power: P = VI = I²R = V²/R. Energy: E = Pt (kWh = kW × h; 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ — the 'unit' on bills). Cost = units × price.
  • Fuse rating just above normal current (P = VI: 3 A covers < 720 W at 240 V). Fuse MELTS when too much current flows (short circuit or overload). Earth wire: metal-case fault → large current to earth → fuse blows. Double insulation needs no earth.
  • Circuit breakers & RCDs: faster, resettable. Mains: 220–240 V AC, 50 Hz.

• Bar magnet: N and S poles; like repel; field lines N→S outside; steel keeps magnetism (permanent), soft iron temporary (electromagnets).
  • Compass needle points along the field; Earth's field enables navigation.
  • Current → circular field (right-hand grip rule); solenoid → bar-magnet-like field; soft-iron core → ELECTROMAGNET, strength ↑ with current, turns/cm, core quality. Uses: bells, relays, cranes, Maglev.
  • Motor effect: F = BIL (max when perpendicular); direction by Fleming's LEFT-hand rule. Motor: coil + commutator reverses current every half-turn → continuous rotation; faster with stronger magnets, more current, more turns.
  • Electromagnetic induction: emf induced when conductor cuts field lines — motion or changing field; size ↑ with speed, field strength, turns. Lenz's law: induced current OPPOSES the change.
  • Generator: coil in field → alternating emf; slip rings (AC) vs split-ring commutator (DC). Transformer: V_p/V_s = N_p/N_s; step-up for transmission (less I²R heat loss); national grid: power station → step-up → grid → step-down → consumers.

• Atom: dense nucleus (protons + neutrons, most of mass) + electrons in shells. Rutherford's gold-foil scattering: most α passed straight (atom mostly empty), few deflected (small positive nucleus), very few bounced back (nucleus massive).
  • Isotopes: same protons, different neutrons — ¹⁴C dating, ⁶⁰Co treatment, ²³⁵U fuel.
  • Radioactive decay is RANDOM and SPONTANEOUS. Radiations: α = helium nucleus — strongly ionising, stopped by paper; β = electron — mm Al; γ = EM wave — needs lead/concrete, undeflected by fields.
  • Decay equations: α → A −4, Z −2; β → A same, Z +1; γ → no change. Conserve mass & atomic numbers.
  • Half-life: time for half the nuclei to decay — CONSTANT per isotope. Graph method: halve a value, read the time gap. Uses by half-life: smoke alarm ²⁴¹Am, tracers ⁹⁹ᵐTc, dating ¹⁴C (5730 y).
  • Fission: ²³⁵U + neutron → fragments + 2–3 neutrons + ~200 MeV; chain reaction controlled by moderator & control rods. Fusion: 2H + 3H → ⁴He + n — powers the Sun; needs ~10⁷°C.
  • Safety: background radiation sources (cosmic, granite, radon, medical); shielding/distance/time; waste deep-stored; irradiated food is NOT radioactive.

• Paper 1 (MCQ): 40 questions, 1 h → 90 s each. Eliminate absurd options; watch unit traps (cm vs m, g vs kg, kW vs W).
  • Paper 2: definitions word-perfect ('the rate of change of momentum'); explain questions want the mechanism (particles/electrons/forces named); calculations need formula → substitution → answer + unit, 3 s.f.
  • Definitions bank: acceleration, average speed, moment, pressure, work, power, efficiency, half-life, isotope, frequency, wavelength, critical angle, centre of gravity.
  • Common mark-scheme phrases: 'because the centre of gravity is lowered/rises', 'electrons are free to move', 'molecules gain kinetic energy and escape from the surface', 'rate of change of momentum', 'induced emf when lines of force are cut'.
  • Check the unit asked (kJ vs J, g vs kg, minutes vs seconds); give vectors a direction when the question says 'velocity' or 'force'.

• Speed: distance travelled per unit time. Velocity: speed in a stated direction. Acceleration: rate of change of velocity. Momentum: mass × velocity.
  • Weight: force of gravity on a mass (W = mg). Density: mass per unit volume. Pressure: force per unit area.
  • Moment: force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Work: force × distance moved in the direction of the force. Power: work done per unit time.
  • Frequency: waves passing a point per second. Wavelength: distance between consecutive in-phase points. Amplitude: maximum displacement from rest.
  • Critical angle: angle of incidence (in denser medium) giving 90° refraction. Half-life: time for half the radioactive nuclei to decay / activity to halve.
  • Latent heat of vaporisation: energy to change 1 kg of liquid to gas at constant temperature. Specific heat capacity: energy to raise 1 kg by 1°C.

• SUVAT: list knowns with signs → select equation with exactly one unknown → solve → check sign makes sense.
  • Momentum collision: total p before = total p after, each side Σmv with signs.
  • Moments: draw pivot, mark all forces & perpendicular distances, CW = ACW.
  • Hooke/graph: k = gradient (F/x); energy = ½Fx = area under line.
  • Calorimetry: E = mcΔθ (or ml); electrical heater: E = VIt. Precautions: lid + insulation, stir, repeat.
  • Circuits: redraw parallel → equivalent R → series sum → total current → back-fill branches. Power: P = VI; cost: kWh × rate.
  • Waves: v = fλ with unit conversion; echo distance = vt/2; T = 1/f.
  • Half-life from table: count ratio (e.g. 800→200 = two halvings); t½ = elapsed ÷ halvings.

olevel/bio5090.b:
• Animal cell: nucleus (controls, contains DNA), cytoplasm (reactions), cell membrane (controls entry/exit, partially permeable), mitochondria (aerobic respiration). Plant adds: cell wall (cellulose, fully permeable, support), chloroplasts (photosynthesis), permanent vacuole (sap — keeps cell rigid).
  • Specialised cells: root hair (long extension → large surface for absorption), red blood (biconcave → large SA, no nucleus → more haemoglobin), sperm (tail, mitochondria), xylem (dead hollow lignified tubes — water transport + support), nerve (long axon), guard cells (kidney-shaped, stomata control).
  • Microscopy: magnification = image size ÷ actual size; 1 mm = 1000 µm; 1 µm = 1000 nm. Convert BEFORE calculating. Electron microscopes: higher magnification/resolution, but specimens dead & in vacuum.
  • Drawing rules: sharp pencil, continuous thin lines, no shading, label lines straight with a ruler.

• Diffusion: net movement from high → low concentration; passive. Faster with bigger gradient, higher temperature, larger surface area. Examples: O₂/CO₂ in lungs & leaves, glucose from gut, mineral ions into roots.
  • Osmosis: diffusion of WATER only, across a partially permeable membrane, from dilute → concentrated solution. Experiments: potato strips in sucrose — mass/length change; Visking tubing models the gut wall.
  • Active transport: movement AGAINST the gradient, needs carrier proteins + ATP (from respiration). Examples: mineral ions into root hairs, glucose from gut into blood, kidney reabsorption. Killed cells stop absorbing → proves ATP needed.
  • Comparing: diffusion needs no membrane proteins or energy; active transport stops at low temperature or with metabolic poisons.

• Carbohydrates: starch TEST = iodine → blue-black; glucose = Benedict's heated → brick-red; sucrose = non-reducing (hydrolyse first with dilute HCl).
  • Proteins: biuret → purple. Fats: ethanol emulsion → cloudy white; or grease spot on paper.
  • Enzymes: protein catalysts; active site fits substrate ('lock and key'); unchanged & reusable, highly specific.
  • Rate factors: temperature — rises to optimum (~37°C) then DENATURED (bonds break, active site shape lost PERMANENTLY); pH — pepsin ~2, amylase ~7, extremes denature; concentration — faster until saturation.
  • Experiments: amylase + starch sampled with iodine; liver catalase + H₂O₂ (frothing, glowing splint); water baths control temperature.
  • Denaturation is NOT melting — losing shape, usually irreversible.

• 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light energy captured by chlorophyll in chloroplasts). Glucose used for: respiration, starch storage, cellulose walls, amino acids (with nitrates), oils.
  • Leaf adaptations: broad flat lamina (large SA), thin (short diffusion distance), palisade mesophyll packed with chloroplasts, stomata (mostly lower epidermis), air spaces, veins, waxy cuticle.
  • Limiting factors: light intensity, CO₂ concentration, temperature — the factor in shortest supply limits the rate. Greenhouse tricks: extra CO₂, artificial light, heating.
  • Starch test: destarch in the dark 24 h FIRST · boil in water · boil in ethanol (water bath — flammable!) to remove chlorophyll · rinse · iodine → blue-black where starch. Variegated leaf: only green parts positive (chlorophyll needed). Masked leaf: light needed. Soda-lime bag: CO₂ needed.
  • Starch is the store because glucose is soluble (would disturb osmosis) and reactive.

• Balanced diet: carbohydrates (energy), proteins (growth/repair), fats (energy store, insulation), vitamins, minerals, water, fibre. Deficiencies: vitamin C → scurvy; vitamin D/Ca → rickets; iron → anaemia; iodine → goitre; protein → kwashiorkor.
  • Canal: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → colon → rectum. Accessory: salivary glands, liver (bile), pancreas (enzymes), gall bladder (stores bile).
  • Mechanical digestion (teeth, churning) increases surface area; chemical digestion = enzymes breaking LARGE insoluble molecules → SMALL soluble ones: amylase (starch → maltose), protease/pepsin (protein → peptides, stomach pH 2), lipase (fat → fatty acids + glycerol), maltase (maltose → glucose).
  • Bile: made in liver, stored in gall bladder, EMULSIFIES fats → larger surface for lipase; ALKALINE → neutralises stomach acid.
  • Villi: huge surface area, one-cell walls, rich capillaries, lacteal (fats). The universal adaptation formula: SA↑ + thin + moist + transport away.
  • Large intestine absorbs water & salts; peristalsis = rhythmic muscle contractions pushing food.

• Heart = double pump: RIGHT → pulmonary artery → lungs (deoxygenated); LEFT → aorta → body (oxygenated). Valves prevent backflow; septum separates circulations.
  • Cardiac cycle: atria contract → ventricles contract ('lub') → relax ('dub'). Coronary arteries feed the heart muscle; blockage → heart attack.
  • Vessels: arteries — thick elastic walls, carry blood AWAY at high pressure; veins — thin walls, VALVES, low pressure return; capillaries — one-cell walls for exchange. 'Artery = away' (pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood!).
  • Blood: red cells (biconcave, haemoglobin + iron, no nucleus), white cells (phagocytes engulf; lymphocytes make antibodies), platelets (clotting — fibrin mesh), plasma (transports glucose, CO₂, urea, hormones, heat).
  • Double circulation advantages: higher pressure to body; separation of oxygenated/deoxygenated blood → efficient O₂ delivery.
  • Lymphatic system drains tissue fluid back; lacteals carry fat.

• Aerobic: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + LOTS of energy (mitochondria).
  • Anaerobic: muscles: glucose → lactic acid + LITTLE energy; oxygen debt = extra O₂ needed afterwards to oxidise lactic acid. Yeast: glucose → ethanol + CO₂ (fermentation — brewing, baking).
  • Exercise response: muscles need more energy → more respiration → O₂ demand & CO₂ production rise → brain raises breathing rate/depth and heart rate.
  • Lungs: trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Alveoli adaptations: millions (huge SA), one-cell walls, moist lining, capillary-wrapped. Exhaled air: more CO₂, less O₂, more water vapour.
  • Smoking damages: tar (cancer, mucus), CO (binds haemoglobin), nicotine (addictive). Diseases: bronchitis, emphysema, lung cancer.
  • Plants: stomata (guard cells bow with water → open), lenticels, leaf air spaces.

• Homeostasis = keeping internal conditions CONSTANT: temperature, blood glucose, water, ions, urea, CO₂. Negative feedback: change detected → response OPPOSES it → return to set point.
  • Temperature: hypothalamus detects; sweat evaporation cools; vasodilation/vasoconstriction of skin vessels; shivering generates heat; hairs trap air; behaviour (shade, clothing).
  • Blood glucose: high → INSULIN → liver/muscles store glucose as glycogen; low → GLUCAGON → glycogen → glucose. Diabetes type 1 (no insulin — injections), type 2 (resistance — diet/exercise). Test: Benedict's.
  • Kidney: glomerulus filters (water, glucose, salts, urea pass; proteins & cells stay); tubule REABSORBS all glucose, most water, some salts; urea + excess → bladder. ADH controls water reabsorption (less water → more ADH). Dialysis mimics filtration.
  • Liver roles: glucose↔glycogen store, deamination (amino acids → urea), alcohol detox, bile production.

• Nervous system: CNS (brain + spinal cord) + peripheral nerves. Neurones: sensory, relay, motor. Impulses travel electrically along axons; synapses work chemically (neurotransmitter, ~1 ms delay).
  • Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neurone → relay (CNS) → motor neurone → effector. FAST, AUTOMATIC, PROTECTIVE.
  • Eye: cornea (refracts), iris/pupil (light control), lens (focuses via ciliary muscles — fat for near, thin for distant), retina (rods: dim/B-W; cones: colour, at fovea), optic nerve. Short sight → diverging lens; long sight → converging lens.
  • Hormones vs nerves: nerves fast/short/precise; hormones slow/long/widespread. Both coordinate.
  • Plant tropisms: shoots +phototropism/−gravitropism; roots +gravitropism/+hydrotropism. Auxin accumulates on shaded side → cells elongate → bend toward light. Gibberellins (stem elongation), ethene (ripening), abscisic acid (stomatal closing, dormancy). Uses: rooting powder, weedkillers, ripening chambers.

• Asexual: one parent, no gametes, identical clones (bacteria fission, yeast budding, runners, tubers). Fast; preserves good traits; no variation.
  • Sexual: gametes fuse (fertilisation) → zygote → VARIED offspring. Variation from meiosis (random assortment, crossing over), random fertilisation, environment.
  • DNA double helix in chromosomes; gene = DNA section for a protein; alleles = alternative forms. Dominant expressed in one copy (capital).
  • Cross method: parental genotypes → gametes (circle) → Punnett square → genotype ratio → phenotype ratio. Monohybrid F₂ = 3:1. Sex determination: XX/XY; P(boy) = ½.
  • Mutation: random DNA change — mostly harmful, occasionally beneficial (basis of evolution).
  • Plant reproduction: anther → pollen; stigma/ovary; insect vs wind pollination; fertilisation → seed + fruit (from ovary); dispersal; germination needs water, oxygen, suitable temperature.
  • Human: FSH (follicle maturation), LH (ovulation), oestrogen/progesterone (lining; the Pill inhibits FSH). Placenta: exchange + barrier — blood never mixes; umbilical cord; amnion.

• Ecosystem = community + habitat. Food chains: arrows = ENERGY direction (grass → grasshopper → frog → snake). Producers → primary consumers (herbivores) → secondary/tertiary (carnivores).
  • ~10% energy passes between levels (lost as heat, movement, uneaten parts) → chains rarely exceed 5 levels.
  • Pyramids of numbers (can invert — one tree, many insects), biomass (usually upright), energy.
  • Carbon cycle: photosynthesis removes CO₂; respiration, combustion, decay return it. Decomposers recycle nutrients. Fossil fuel burning → CO₂ rise → greenhouse effect → global warming.
  • Nitrogen cycle: nitrogen-fixing bacteria (legume root nodules, lightning, Haber) → nitrates; nitrifying bacteria (ammonium → nitrates); denitrifying (nitrates → N₂); decomposers (protein → ammonia).
  • Eutrophication chain: fertiliser runoff → algal bloom → light blocked → plants die → decomposers multiply → O₂ depleted → fish die. Pesticides bioaccumulate/biomagnify (DDT).
  • Population growth: sigmoid curve — lag → exponential → plateau at carrying capacity K. Limiting factors: food, disease, space.

• Bacteria in food: yoghurt (Lactobacillus: lactose → lactic acid, clots milk), cheese (rennet + bacteria), vinegar (ethanol → acetic acid), bread (yeast CO₂).
  • Genetic engineering outline: extract human insulin gene → insert into bacterial plasmid → bacteria clone & express it. Cheap, pure, ethical.
  • Drug development: modelling, cell tests, animal trials, double-blind clinical trials, peer review. Antibiotics kill bacteria only (not viruses); overuse → resistant strains (MRSA) — finish the course.
  • Agriculture: selective breeding (choose parents with desired traits over generations), fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation vs organic trade-offs.

• Command words: 'state' = one fact; 'describe' = sequence; 'explain' = mechanism with 'because/so that'; 'compare' = both sides; 'suggest' = apply to a novel situation.
  • Every 'adaptation' answer: feature → therefore → benefit ('villi increase surface area → faster absorption').
  • Practical questions (P6): variables (independent/dependent/controlled ×3), method, expected results + conclusion, evaluation (repeats & mean, insulation, control group).
  • Food test colours: Benedict's brick-red · iodine blue-black · biuret purple · ethanol milky.
  • Drawings: pencil, no shading, ruler labels, correct proportions; plan diagrams show NO individual cells.
  • Definitions: diffusion, osmosis, active transport, photosynthesis, respiration, homeostasis, negative feedback, trophic level, allele, dominant, variation, excretion vs egestion, transpiration, peristalsis.

• Diffusion: net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration down a gradient. Osmosis: diffusion of water through a partially permeable membrane from dilute to more concentrated solution. Active transport: movement against a gradient using energy.
  • Photosynthesis: green plants make glucose from CO₂ and water using light energy. Respiration: release of energy from glucose in living cells.
  • Homeostasis: maintaining constant internal conditions despite external changes. Negative feedback: response counteracting a change to restore the set point.
  • Allele: alternative form of a gene. Dominant: expressed with one copy. Variation: differences between individuals of a species.
  • Trophic level: feeding level in a food chain. Transpiration: loss of water vapour from leaves driving water up xylem.
  • Excretion: removal of metabolic waste (urea, CO₂). Egestion: removal of undigested food — NOT excretion.

olevel/math4024.b:
• Types: natural, integers, rational, irrational (√2, π), real. Prime = exactly two factors; 1 not prime; 2 only even prime.
  • HCF/LCM by prime factors: HCF = lowest powers of common primes; LCM = highest powers of all primes. HCF × LCM = a × b.
  • Fractions ⇄ decimals ⇄ percentages; % change = change/original × 100 — original is the base. Reverse %: divide by the multiplier.
  • Ratio sharing: total parts → one part → shares. Bounds: value ± half the rounding unit (upper exclusive). Combining: × → U×U/L×L; ÷ → U÷L/L÷U.
  • Standard form a × 10ⁿ (1 ≤ a < 10). Indices: aᵐaⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ; a^(m/n) = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. Surds: combine like terms only; rationalise by × surd/surd.
  • Estimate: 1 s.f. everything, then compute.

• Expansion: FOIL; (a±b)² = a² ± 2ab + b². Factorising: HCF first, then ×→c +→b pair; a²−b² = (a−b)(a+b).
  • Linear equations: same operation both sides; clear fractions by ×LCM. Word problems: define → form → solve → answer in words with units.
  • Simultaneous: elimination (opposite signs → add; same → subtract); substitution when a lone variable exists. Verify in BOTH equations.
  • Inequalities: flip the sign when × or ÷ by a negative. Number line: open < >, closed ≤ ≥.
  • Sequences: nth term = dn + (a₁ − d); quadratic sequences have constant second differences.
  • Variation: direct y = kx, inverse y = k/x; find k, then use. Rates: speed, density, pressure.

• Solve: factorise (try first) → formula (signs!) → completing the square (x + b/2)² − (b/2)².
  • Discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac: >0 two roots, =0 repeated (touch), <0 none. 'Equal roots' → Δ = 0 → solve for the parameter.
  • Root relationships: sum = −b/a, product = c/a — build equations from roots and CHECK solutions.
  • Parabola: c = y-intercept; axis x = −b/2a; vertex from completing the square; a > 0 minimum. Sketch: roots + intercept + vertex.
  • Lines: gradient m = Δy/Δx; y = mx + c; point–gradient form; parallel m equal; perpendicular m₂ = −1/m₁; midpoint & distance.
  • Travel graphs: d–t gradient = speed; s–t gradient = acceleration, AREA = distance.
  • Functions: f(x); composite fg(x) — INSIDE first; inverse: make x the subject.

• Angle facts: line 180°, point 360°, vertically opposite equal; parallels: alternate (Z) equal, corresponding (F) equal, co-interior (C) 180°. Triangle sum 180°.
  • Polygons: exterior sum 360°; regular exterior = 360/n; interior = 180 − exterior; interior sum = (n−2)×180°.
  • Congruence: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS. Similarity: lengths ×k, areas ×k², volumes ×k³.
  • Circle theorems (six): semicircle 90°; centre = 2 × circumference (same arc); same segment equal; cyclic quad opposite 180°; tangent ⊥ radius; alternate segment. Equal radii → isosceles triangles; NAME the theorem as your reason.
  • Constructions: perpendicular bisector, angle bisector, 60°/90° — leave ALL arcs visible.
  • Loci: perpendicular bisector (two points), angle bisector (two lines), circle (fixed distance). Shade regions.

• Area: triangle ½bh, parallelogram bh, trapezium ½(a+b)h, circle πr²; semicircle perimeter = πr + 2r (add the diameter!).
  • Sector = θ/360 of circle: arc = (θ/360)2πr, area = (θ/360)πr²; segment = sector − triangle.
  • Volume: prism (cross-section × length), cylinder πr²h, cone ⅓πr²h, sphere ⁴⁄₃πr³, pyramid ⅓ × base × h. 1 L = 1000 cm³; 1 m³ = 1000 L.
  • Surface: cylinder 2πrh + 2πr²; cone πrl + πr², l = √(r² + h²); sphere 4πr²; composites share NO internal faces.
  • Similar solids: length k → area k² → volume k³.

• Pythagoras; 3D diagonal d² = a² + b² + c².
  • SOH CAH TOA; inverses find angles; check DEG mode; exact values 30/45/60.
  • Elevation = depression (alternate angles); draw the horizontal FIRST.
  • Bearings: three figures, clockwise from North; reverse ± 180°; North line at EVERY point; north = d cos θ, east = d sin θ.
  • Sine rule a/sinA = b/sinB — needs an opposite pair; ambiguous case: check θ and 180°−θ.
  • Cosine rule — SSS or SAS. Keep 4 s.f. in working.
  • Area = ½ab sinC (included angle). Sketch first, always.

• Column vectors add component-wise; magnitude √(x² + y²). AB = b − a; midpoint (a+b)/2.
  • Proofs: collinear ⇔ scalar multiple AND a shared point. Parallel ⇔ multiple.
  • Transformations — describe FULLY: reflection (mirror line), rotation (centre + angle + direction), translation (column vector), enlargement (SF + centre).
  • Negative enlargement passes through the centre; 0 < k < 1 shrinks; area × k², volume × k³.
  • Unknown transformation: same size → translation; flipped → perpendicular bisector; resized → k from lengths, centre from rays.

• Sampling: random (least bias), systematic, stratified (proportional), quota, convenience (most biased).
  • Averages: mean = Σx/n; median = middle of ORDERED data; mode = most frequent. Mean outlier-sensitive; median robust; mode for categories.
  • Grouped data: estimated mean Σfx/Σf with midpoints; modal class = highest bar.
  • Cumulative frequency: plot (upper boundary, running total); smooth curve; median at n/2, quartiles n/4 & 3n/4; IQR = UQ − LQ.
  • Histograms: frequency DENSITY = frequency ÷ class width; area = frequency.
  • Probability: complement 1 − P(A); trees: multiply along, add across; without replacement updates counts; 'at least one' → 1 − P(none); Venn: P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B); conditional P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).

• 4024 P1: 24 short questions, 2 h → ~5 min each. P2: 10 structured; parts chain — error carried forward credited, NEVER blank a later part.
  • Show every line of working — method marks are the currency; correct answer without working can score ZERO.
  • 3 s.f. final answers; keep 4+ s.f. intermediate; units on answers; money 2 d.p.
  • Diagram questions: redraw and label — most geometry/trig errors die at the sketch.
  • 'Show that': treat the given answer as untouchable; derive it line by line.
  • Calculator: DEG mode; bracket negatives; write intermediates before rounding.
  • 10-minute review: missed parts ('perimeter AND area'), sign sanity, requested form (standard form, exact surd, simplest ratio).

• HCF/LCM: highest common factor / lowest common multiple. Irrational: not writable as a fraction. Standard form: a × 10ⁿ, 1 ≤ a < 10.
  • Gradient: change in y ÷ change in x. Discriminant: b² − 4ac, decides real roots.
  • Hypotenuse: side opposite the right angle. Bearing: clockwise from North, three figures.
  • Median: middle of ordered data. IQR: upper − lower quartile. Mutually exclusive: cannot happen together.
  • Enlargement: scaling by k about a centre. Similar: equal angles, proportional sides.

olevel/isl2058.b:
• Articles (Iman): Allah (Tawhid — no partners), angels (Jibril — revelation; Mika'il — provision; Israfil — trumpet; Izra'il — death; Kiraman Katibin — recorders), revealed books (Suhuf Ibrahim, Tawrah, Zabur, Injil, Qur'an — final & preserved), prophets (25 named; final = Muhammad ﷺ), the Last Day, divine decree Qadar.
  • Pillars: Shahadah (foundation) · Salah (5 daily; wudu; Jumu'ah; rak'ah: Fajr 2, Maghrib 3, others 4) · Zakah (2.5% above nisab held one lunar year; recipients per At-Tawbah 60) · Sawm (Ramadan; exceptions: illness, travel, pregnancy; fidya/kaffara) · Hajj (once if able: ihram, tawaf, sa'i, Arafat — the essential rite, Muzdalifah, Mina, sacrifice, farewell tawaf).
  • Compare: which pillar is daily/monthly/annual/lifetime; which tests wealth vs patience.

• Revelation: began in Cave Hira (610 CE) via Jibril; 23 years; Arabic; 'Qur'an' = recitation.
  • Compilation: memorised + fragments in the Prophet's life; Abu Bakr ordered collection after Yamamah (632); Uthman standardised the codex and sent copies to the provinces — preventing division.
  • Structure: 114 surahs (86 Makkan — short, tawhid-focused; 28 Madinan — law & society), 6236 verses, 30 juz'. Longest: Al-Baqarah; first revealed: 'Iqra' (Al-Alaq).
  • Themes to quote: Tawhid (Ikhlas 112), Yusuf (12 — patience & forgiveness), the Hereafter (Ya-Sin 36), parents (17:23), unity (3:103).
  • Tajwid preserves recitation; translations convey meanings, not the Qur'an itself.

• Hadith = saying/action/approval of the Prophet ﷺ; Sunnah = his way of life. Second authority — explains the Qur'an (how to pray, zakah details, character).
  • Structure: isnad (chain) + matn (text). Collections: Sahih Bukhari & Sahih Muslim most authentic, then Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah.
  • Scholars graded narrators for truthfulness, memory, continuity — fabricated (mawdu') reports rejected, preserving purity.
  • Key hadith: 'Actions are by intentions' (Bukhari 1) · 'None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself' · 'The best of you are the best in character' · 'Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim'.
  • Sunnah never contradicts the Qur'an — it elaborates it.

• Born Makkah 570 CE (Year of the Elephant), Banu Hashim (Quraysh); father Abdullah died before birth; mother Aminah died when he was 6; raised by grandfather Abdul Muttalib, then uncle Abu Talib.
  • Known as Al-Amin (the trustworthy); married Khadijah (first believer) at 25; settled the Black Stone dispute at 35.
  • First revelation 610 CE in Cave Hira; 3 years of secret preaching, then openly: worship Allah, reject false gods.
  • Persecution: 3-year boycott of Banu Hashim; deaths of Khadijah & Abu Talib (Year of Sorrow, 619); Taif rejection (stoned — answered with compassion); Isra & Miraj (621 — five prayers gifted).
  • Pledges of Aqabah (621–622): 12 then 75 men & 2 women from Yathrib pledged faith & protection.

• Hijrah 622 CE (Year 1 of the Islamic calendar): the Prophet ﷺ & Abu Bakr hid in Cave Thawr 3 days; Ali slept as decoy; arrival at Quba — Masjid Quba; the camel's choice fixed the mosque site in Yathrib (Madinah).
  • Constitution of Madinah: one ummah — Muslims, Jews & pagans: mutual defence, religious freedom, sanctuary. First written constitution of a plural state.
  • Masjid Nabawi: prayer, education, court, government. Mu'akhat: each Muhajir paired with an Ansari — shared homes & wealth.
  • Battles: Badr (624 — 313 vs 1000, divine help, Qur'an 3:123) · Uhud (625 — archers left the pass; lesson: obedience) · Khandaq (627 — trench by Salman al-Farsi) · Hudaybiyyah (628 — 10-year peace; 'clear victory' 48:1; da'wah opened) · Conquest of Makkah (630 — general amnesty, idols destroyed) · Hunayn & Tabuk.
  • Farewell Sermon (632, Arafat): sanctity of life & property, riba forbidden, women's rights, Muslim brotherhood. The Prophet ﷺ passed away 632, aged 63, after appointing Abu Bakr to lead prayer.

• Abu Bakr (632–634), as-Siddiq: Ridda wars (Musaylamah defeated by Khalid ibn Walid), false prophets crushed, zakah refusers fought; ordered the Qur'an's compilation.
  • Umar (634–644), al-Farooq: conquests — Persia, Syria, Egypt; Jerusalem surrendered to him personally. Administration: diwan, hijri calendar, Bait ul-Mal, police, canals, new cities (Kufa, Basra, Fustat). Martyred 644.
  • Uthman (644–656), Dhun-Nurayn: standard Qur'anic codex to the provinces; first navy; North Africa, Armenia, Cyprus. Unrest over appointments; martyred 656 while reading the Qur'an.
  • Ali (656–661): Camel & Siffin (arbitration); Khawarij emerged; capital Kufa; martyred 661 by Ibn Muljam.
  • Assessment: unprecedented just expansion; covenant of Umar protected Jerusalem's Christians; administration copied by later empires.

• Qur'an — primary; ~500 legal verses (ibadat & mu'amalat).
  • Sunnah — details: prayer postures, zakah rates, prohibitions. Qur'an commands prayer; Sunnah shows HOW.
  • Ijma' — consensus; 'My ummah never agrees on error'. Examples: Qur'an's collection, apostasy rulings.
  • Qiyas — analogy on shared effective cause (illah): wine's prohibition extends to all intoxicants.
  • Subsidiary: istihsan, maslahah mursalah (public interest), urf (custom), istishab.
  • Schools: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali (Sunni), Ja'fari (Shia) — 'difference of opinion is a mercy' within the framework.

olevel/isl2058.t: 8. Islam in the modern world & ethics
olevel/isl2058.b:
• Riba: money must not breed money without risk. Modern answers: murabahah, mudarabah, musharakah, ijara, sukuk; ethical screening (no alcohol, gambling, weapons).
  • Family: marriage = contract with consent & mahr; 'the best of you is best to his family'; kindness to parents (17:23 — say not even 'uff'); children's rights; divorce permitted but 'most hated of permitted things'.
  • Business: honest weights (Mutaffifin), disclose defects, honour contracts, avoid gharar & maysir.
  • Society: 'no superiority of Arab over non-Arab'; sanctity of life (5:32); sadaqah & waqf (Islam invented the charitable trust); neighbour rights; hospitality.
  • Contemporary: organ donation permitted by many scholars (necessities permit prohibitions); genetic engineering for cure, not 'playing God'; verify before sharing news (49:6); jihad = primarily spiritual striving; terrorism condemned — 'whoever kills an innocent kills humanity'.
  • Interfaith: People of the Book under covenant protection; shared prophets Abraham, Moses, Jesus (Isa — miracle-worker by Allah's leave, not divine).

• Order of events: first revelation 610 · public preaching 613 · boycott 616–619 · Isra Miraj 621 · pledges of Aqabah 621/622 · Hijrah 622 · Badr 624 · Uhud 625 · Khandaq 627 · Hudaybiyyah 628 · conquest of Makkah 630 · Farewell Sermon & passing 632.
  • Describe templates: the Hijrah (reasons: assassination plot, Yathrib invitation; events: cave, Quba, constitution, brotherhood; results: Islamic state, calendar begins). Badr (causes, angels 3:123, effects: prestige). Hudaybiyyah (terms: 10-year truce, return this year, Umrah next; significance: da'wah flourished, Khalid & Amr embraced Islam).
  • Caliphs table: Abu Bakr — ridda, compilation; Umar — conquests, diwan, calendar; Uthman — codex, navy; Ali — Kufa, arbitration lessons.
  • Personalities: Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Umar (justice), Uthman, Ali, Bilal (equality), Salman (trench), Zayd ibn Thabit (compiler).

• Every application answer: quote a verse/hadith WITH source → why it matters → 3 concrete steps → conclusion. Four layers.
  • Cheating: 'Whoever deceives us is not one of us' (Muslim) · long-term harm: knowledge without barakah, corrupt character · advice: prepare early, Allah sees, seek help, make dua.
  • Disrespectful child: 17:23 + 'Paradise lies under the mother's feet' (Nasa'i) · speak gently, help with chores, make dua, never abandon them in old age.
  • Business fraud: 'The truthful merchant is with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs' (Tirmidhi) · disclose defects, fair scales, accept returns — trust brings barakah.
  • Interest temptation: 2:278–279 declares war on riba · seek scholarships, family help, halal financing, part-time work.
  • Social media rumour: 'Enough sin to repeat all you hear' (Abu Dawud) + 49:6 verification · pause, check sources, speak good or stay silent.

• P1 rewards SEQUENCE and DETAIL: dates, names, places, numbers. Learn timelines as chains.
  • 'Describe' = narrate in order with specifics; 'Explain the importance' = effects → significance. 4 marks ≈ 4 developed points.
  • P2: read the scenario twice; identify the teaching (tawhid, honesty, kindness, justice, patience); weave the scenario details in — never answer generically.
  • Memorise 15–20 short quotes with sources — sourced quotes score higher.
  • Two-sided questions: Islamic ruling first → modern context → practical halal alternative → committed conclusion.
  • Structure: intro naming the theme, paragraphs per teaching, conclusion sentence.

olevel/chem0620.b:
• Particle theory: solids (fixed, vibrate), liquids (slide), gases (free, fast) — explains shape, volume, compression, diffusion.
  • Diffusion: NH₃ (lighter) diffuses faster than HCl (heavy) — white ring of NH₄Cl forms nearer the HCl end of the tube.
  • Separation toolkit: filtration, crystallisation, evaporation, simple & fractional distillation, separating funnel, chromatography (Rf = spot ÷ solvent front).
  • Atomic structure: p/n/e; isotopes (¹⁴C dating, ⁶⁰Co treatment, ²³⁵U/²³⁸U); electrons in shells 2, 8, 8; configuration writes like 2, 8, 1.

• Mole conversions: n = m/M = cV = V/24 (gas) · % yield & % purity · empirical → molecular formula.
  • Ionic: transfer, lattice, conducts molten/aqueous, high m.p. Covalent: sharing; simple molecular (low m.p.) vs giant (diamond, graphite, SiO₂ — graphite conducts: delocalised electrons between layers). Metallic: sea of electrons → conducts, malleable.
  • Structure → property questions: always link the particle behaviour (delocalised electrons/free ions/giant lattice) to the observed property.

• Electrolyte = molten/aqueous ionic compound or acid; non-electrolytes: sugar, ethanol.
  • Brine: H₂ cathode, Cl₂ anode, NaOH left. Molten PbBr₂: Pb cathode, Br₂ anode.
  • Electroplating: object = cathode, silver/copper anode, electrolyte of the plating metal. Half-equations with e⁻ balance.
  • Applications: Al extraction (molten Al₂O₃ in cryolite — lowers m.p.), electrorefining of Cu, hydrogen fuel cells vs rechargeable cells.

• Exo: combustion, neutralisation, respiration. Endo: thermal decomposition, photosynthesis. Energy profiles: Ea peak, ΔH gap.
  • Bond energy estimate: ΔH = broken − formed. Calorimetry: q = mcΔT, heat loss makes magnitude small.
  • Rates: collision theory; catalyst lowers Ea, unchanged at end; same final volume with/without catalyst.
  • Reversible reactions & dynamic equilibrium: closed container, rates equal. Le Chatelier + conditions of Contact/Haber processes (Fe/V₂O₅ catalysts, 450°C).

• pH scale, indicators, strong vs weak acids; oxide types (acidic, basic, amphoteric Al₂O₃, neutral CO/H₂O).
  • Salt preparation: soluble (titration / excess + crystallise) vs insoluble (precipitate, filter, wash, dry).
  • Ionic tests: NH₄⁺ (warm NaOH → NH₃), Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺/Cu²⁺ colours with NaOH, Cl⁻/Br⁻/I⁻ with AgNO₃ + dilute HNO₃, SO₄²⁻ with BaCl₂ + HCl, CO₃²⁻ (acid → CO₂ → limewater milky).
  • Titration calculations: mol ratio chain, working shown, 3 s.f.

• Group I/II/VII/VIII trends with reasons (electron distance/shielding). Transition metals: colour, variable valency, catalysts.
  • Reactivity series → displacement & extraction method (electrolysis above zinc; carbon reduction below). Blast furnace chemistry. Alloys: steel types, brass, bronze, solder. Rusting needs water + O₂; galvanising sacrificial.
  • Organic: alkanes (burn, substitute), alkenes (bromine water test, addition, polymerisation), alcohols (fermentation C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂), carboxylic acids (weak, fizz carbonates), esters (fruit smells, solvent/perfume), polymers (addition & condensation — nylon, Terylene), cracking feedstock.
  • P6/ATP skills: read burettes/thermometers, plot & interpret graphs, describe tests, evaluate plans.

olevel/eng1123.b:
• 2 hours, 50 marks = 50%: Section A comprehension of a narrative (~900 words, 25 marks): explicit answers (locate & copy-adapt), implicit/inference questions, language analysis ('How does the writer create tension?'). Section B (25): summary (max 150 words) + a short response on implicit meanings/attitudes.
  • Own-words rule: paraphrase unless told to quote. 1 mark = one distinct point; a 2-mark answer needs two separate points, not one repeated.
  • Inference formula: 'This suggests ___ because the text says "___"' — claim + evidence. Never write the inference and forget the 'because'.
  • Language questions: quote → technique (imagery/verb choice/contrast/rhetorical question) → effect on reader. Four steps, always.
  • Timing: ~55 min Section A, 55 min Section B. Never let the summary eat Q3 time.

• Read the FOCUS LINE first: only points answering it count — everything else loses marks even if true.
  • Routine: underline 12–15 relevant points in rough → convert each to your own words (change word class, e.g. noun→verb) → combine into ONE paragraph ≤150 words → connectives (furthermore, consequently, however) → no examples, no opinions, no repetition.
  • Own-words proof: copied phrases score zero for language; the examiner can see the original through the window of your paragraph.
  • Count words: 140–150 is the sweet spot — under 130 usually means you missed points; over 150 = penalty.

• 2 hours, 50 marks = 50%: Section A Directed Writing (25) — ONE compulsory task from stimulus text(s); respond 250–350 words; discursive/argumentative/persuasive. Section B Composition (25) — ONE of four titles (2 descriptive, 2 narrative), 350–450 words.
  • Directed writing checklist: correct format · audience-appropriate register · at least THREE stimulus facts woven in (marks are allocated to them) · developed paragraphs · clear conclusion/recommendation.
  • Paragraph engine: Point → stimulus evidence → explanation → mini-conclusion. Five focused paragraphs beat ten thin ones.
  • Word discipline: 250–350 DW / 350–450 comp. Counting matters — examiners stop marking beyond the limit.

• Speech: direct address, rhetorical questions, rule of three, emotive vocab, formal greeting & closing thanks.
  • Formal letter: addresses, date, 'Dear Sir/Madam', subject heading, Yours faithfully + full name. No contractions.
  • Report/proposal: title, To/From/Date, introduction stating purpose, findings with headings, recommendations ('It is recommended that…').
  • Article: headline, byline, engaging opening hook, subheadings optional, balanced tone for school magazines.
  • Register markers: formal = full forms, polite modals (would/could), no slang; informal = contractions, exclamations, idioms, direct address.

• Show don't tell: 'His knuckles whitened around the letter' beats 'He was nervous'.
  • Five senses beyond sight: sound, smell, texture, temperature. Two per paragraph is plenty.
  • Sentence variety rhythm: long flowing sentence → short punch ('Silence.') → medium. Variety is the style band's currency.
  • Zoom structure: wide establishing shot → narrow to one detail → the focal moment → pull back with a resonant final image.
  • Pathetic fallacy & symbolism done subtly: weather mirrors mood once, not every line.
  • Strong verbs over adverbs: 'sprinted' not 'ran quickly'; 'devoured' not 'ate hungrily'.

• Hook in line one: in medias res action, dialogue, a shocking short sentence, a question.
  • Structure arc: setup → complication → rising tension → climax → resolution (or deliberate echo of opening). Plan it in 5 minutes before writing.
  • Dialogue punctuation drill: new speaker = new line; comma inside quotes ('I know,' she said); interrupted speech = dash.
  • Tension tools: short sentences, sensory narrowing (time slows), withheld information, a ticking clock.
  • Endings: resolution, twist, circular echo, or open question — never 'and then I woke up'.

• Subject–verb agreement (The list of items IS…), tense consistency within paragraphs, pronoun reference clarity.
  • Punctuation: apostrophes (its/it's, plural possessives girls'), commas after introductory clauses, semicolons joining related independent clauses.
  • Common errors to hunt in review: their/there/they're · your/you're · could of → could have · less vs fewer · misplaced modifiers ('Running down the road, the bag fell').
  • Spelling shortlist: definitely, separate, necessary, accommodation, embarrass, occurrence, questionnaire, maintenance.
  • Leave 5 minutes to proofread — accuracy is a scored band, and most marks are lost to slips, not ideas.

• Content (what): relevance to the title, developed ideas, stimulus facts used — plan first, write second.
  • Language (how): register control, vocabulary range, sentence variety, idiomatic/natural phrasing — upgraded verbs + varied openings.
  • Structure (shape): clear paragraphs, cohesion (linking words that mean something), opening & closing strength.
  • Accuracy: spelling, punctuation, grammar — proofread pass mandatory.
  • The difference between 17 and 22 is rarely ideas — it's accuracy + register + development depth.

olevel/eng0500.b:
• 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%: Q1(a–e) comprehension of Text A (15) · Q1(f) summary of Text B ≤120 words (15) · Q2 language analysis 200–300 words (20) · Q3 extended response 250–350 words in a set format (30).
  • Texts share ONE theme in an insert — skim all three first (5 min) so Q3's format choice is informed.
  • Timing (Cambridge guide): 15–20 min Q1(a–e) · 20 min Q1(f) · 35 min Q2 · 40 min Q3. Q3 = 30/80 — the paper's engine; protect its time.
  • Q1(a–e): own words, one point per mark, anchor with short quotes where asked.

• Quote → name technique → what it means → effect on the reader. Four steps, every time, in continuous prose.
  • Three examples from EACH specified paragraph; pick striking verbs and contrasts, not the first three words.
  • Technique bank: metaphor/simile, personification, sibilance, alliteration, hyperbole, rhetorical question, tricolon, irony, onomatopoeia, emotive diction.
  • Effect language that scores: 'creates tension', 'suggests vulnerability', 'makes the destruction feel alive', 'positions the reader to sympathise' — never just 'it makes it interesting'.

• ≤120 words, one paragraph, own words, focus-line only, connectives. Cross out rough notes — examiners check selection AND re-expression.
  • Twelve points in rough → combine overlapping → 100–118 words final. Under 100 = missed points; over 120 = penalty.
  • Own-words conversion tricks: noun↔verb swap ('destruction' → 'destroyed'), synonym chains ('angry' → 'furious' → 'incensed'), restructuring clauses.

• Uses Text C ideas in a REQUIRED format: letter, report, journal, speech, interview, article, review, dialogue. Format features earn direct marks.
  • Format signatures: journal (dates + reflection, first person) · interview (alternating Q&A, scene-setting) · report (headings, impersonal) · letter (address, salutation, sign-off) · speech (direct address, rhetorical questions).
  • 250–350 words; develop TWO–THREE Text C ideas with your own elaboration — pure copying caps you low.
  • Read the bullet instructions on Q3: they tell you exactly which ideas to develop.

• Section A (40): evaluate two stimulus texts with opposing views; paragraph engine = idea from text → your evaluation → developed example. BOTH texts must appear for the top band.
  • Section B (40): one of four descriptive/narrative titles — same craft as composition: hook, zoom structure, tension arc, varied sentences, proofread.
  • Timing: 40 min Section A · 70 min Section B · 10 min review.
  • Top-band secret: a clear personal judgement ('While X argues convincingly that…, the stronger case is… because…').

• Pack: black pens ×2, pencil, ruler, eraser; no dictionary allowed in 0500.
  • First 5 minutes: skim insert, note Q3 format, plan Section B choice while answering Q1.
  • Every answer: check the exact instruction (own words? quote? how many words?).
  • Last 10 minutes: word counts (Q1f ≤120, Q3 250–350), format features present, spelling sweep of first lines (examiners read these first).

olevel/eng0510.b:
• Count-in Speaking (most common): Core = P1 Reading & Writing + P3 Listening + P5 Speaking; Extended = P2 + P4 + P6. Extended papers are harder and uncap grades.
  • Reading: note-completion (NO MORE THAN THREE words — copy the instruction each time), matching headings, MCQ, short answers. Questions mostly follow text order.
  • Writing: informal email/letter + a more formal task (article/report/review); tone must match the named audience.
  • Listening: heard TWICE; read questions in the pause before each hearing; answers usually come in order; spelling of copied words counts.
  • Speaking: warm-up questions → topic card (speak 1–2 min: opinion → reason → example) → discussion with the examiner (agree/disagree politely, extend answers).

• Reading: skim for gist (2 min), scan for detail with keywords from the question; for matching tasks, eliminate used options.
  • Informal writing: contractions, friendly openers (Hi Sam,), phrasal verbs, exclamations; cover ALL three bullet points in the task.
  • Formal writing: no contractions, full forms, polite requests ('I would be grateful if…'), passive constructions for impersonal tone.
  • Listening: underline keywords in questions; first hearing = answer, second = check; numbers, names and spellings said slowly are being dictated — write them exactly.
  • Speaking fluency frames: 'In my opinion… because…', 'For example…', 'On the other hand…', 'That's a good point, but…'.

• Writing MORE THAN THREE words in note-completion — automatic mark loss.
  • Informal register leaking into formal tasks (gonna, wanna, slang).
  • Ignoring a bullet point in the writing task — content marks are per bullet.
  • Silent gaps in speaking — use filler frames rather than silence; fluency scores higher than perfection.
  • Leaving blanks in listening — never; a guessed word can score.

olevel/acc7707.b:
• DEAD CLIC: Debits = Expenses, Assets, Drawings; Credits = Liabilities, Income, Capital. Every transaction: ≥1 debit + equal credit.
  • Books of prime entry: sales journal (credit sales), purchases journal, sales returns, purchases returns, cash book (receipts & payments with discounts columns), petty cash book (imprest system: fixed float topped up by the amount spent).
  • Ledger posting: totals from day books to sales/purchases ledger control accounts; individual entries to personal accounts.
  • Trial balance: checks ARITHMETIC only. Errors it MISSES: omission, commission, original entry, complete reversal, principle. Errors it FINDS: one-sided items (suspense account).
  • Suspense account routine: correct each error by journal; post to suspense; suspense must return to zero.

• Bank reconciliation order: (1) update the cash book for items in the statement only — direct debits, standing orders, bank charges, credit transfers, dishonoured cheques, interest; (2) reconciliation statement: balance per bank ± timing — add uncredited deposits, subtract unpresented cheques → corrected cash book balance.
  • Updated cash book first is the #1 exam rule — marks flow from it.
  • Control accounts: sales ledger control = total trade receivables; purchases ledger control = trade payables. Sources: day books + cash book columns.
  • Contra entries appear on BOTH control accounts (same amount). Credit sales → debit SLCA; receipts → credit SLCA; irrecoverable debts & discounts allowed → credit SLCA.
  • Control accounts check the ledgers, locate errors in individual accounts, and provide instant receivables/payables totals for the SOFP.

• Straight line: (cost − residual) ÷ useful life — same charge yearly, popular for buildings. Reducing balance: net book value × % — higher early charges, matches falling efficiency/value.
  • Revaluation model: revalue to fair value, surplus → revaluation reserve (non-distributable).
  • Adjustments drill: accruals (owed → add to expense, liability), prepayments (paid ahead → deduct, asset), irrecoverable debts (expense; remove from receivables), provision for doubtful debts (% of receivables — expense the INCREASE), depreciation, goods for own use (drawings), inventory errors.
  • Capital vs revenue expenditure: improve/extend = capital (asset); repair/run = revenue (expense). Getting this wrong distorts profit AND assets.

• Income statement: revenue − returns = net revenue; opening inventory + purchases + carriage inwards − returns − closing inventory = COGS; gross profit − expenses (with each adjustment applied) = profit for the year. Present in the standard Cambridge format — headings earn marks.
  • SOFP: non-current assets at NBV (cost − accumulated depreciation) + current assets (inventory, receivables − provision, prepayments, bank/cash) − current liabilities (payables, accruals, overdraft, bank loan due) = net current assets; financed by: capital − drawings + profit.
  • Partnerships: appropriation account after income statement — salaries & interest on capital (credited), interest on drawings (charged), residual by profit-sharing ratio; each partner has a CURRENT account (salary, interest, share, drawings).
  • Companies: share capital (ordinary/preference), share premium, debentures (loan interest is an EXPENSE, not appropriation), dividends (final proposed = liability), reserves.
  • Clubs & societies: receipts & payments account (cash summary) + subscriptions account (paid, owing, in advance) → income statement for surplus.
  • Manufacturing: prime cost (direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses) + factory overheads = cost of production → transfers to trading account.

• Incomplete records toolkit: control-account reconstruction to find missing figures, total accounts (e.g. sales = opening receivables + receipts + closing adjustments), markup → margin conversions, cash summaries.
  • Mark-up on cost vs margin on selling: margin = markup ÷ (100 + markup). Given one, convert before using.
  • Ratios & what they MEASURE: gross margin (pricing/cost control), net margin (expense control), ROCE (profitability vs capital employed), current ratio (liquidity; acid test excludes inventory), asset turnover (efficiency), gearing (risk: debt ÷ capital employed), receivables/payables days (working capital cycle).
  • Ratio answers must COMPARE (previous year / another business / industry) before concluding — a naked ratio is half marks.
  • Limitations: window dressing, inflation, one-off items, accounting policy choices, seasonal timing.

• Paper 2 = 120 marks, 1 h 45 → ~52 s/mark. Structured compulsory questions: state formats cold (income statement, SOFP, bank reconciliation, control account, appropriation).
  • OWN-FIGURE RULE: a wrong figure with correct method still earns method marks — and later parts using your own earlier figure keep earning. Never leave a part blank because an earlier number went wrong.
  • Working column: show every calculation beside the statement line — method marks live there.
  • Presentation credit: ruled lines, headings, $ signs, dates ('for the year ended…'), 'workings' labels.
  • MCQ traps: items that affect BOTH suspense and one ledger, accrual vs prepayment direction, markup/margin conversion, carriage inwards (COGS) vs outwards (selling expense).

olevel/bus7115.b:
• Entrepreneur qualities: initiative, risk-taking, organisation, creativity, decision-making, perseverance. Business plan purpose: planning tool + persuading lenders/investors (contents: market, finance, operations, people, cash flow forecast).
  • Sole trader: full control, keep profits, easy setup — BUT unlimited liability, no continuity, limited capital.
  • Partnership: shared skills/capital/risks — but unlimited liability (ordinary), shared profits, possible disputes. Deed of partnership covers capital, profit share, dispute rules.
  • Private limited company (Ltd): limited liability, separate legal identity, continuity, easier capital — but formation legalities, accounts disclosure, loss of control, dividends shared.
  • Franchise: proven brand + support vs fees + rules. Public corporations & multinationals features.
  • Choosing factors: capital needed, liability attitude, control desired, continuity, secrecy, expansion plans.

• Market research: primary (surveys, interviews, observations, test marketing — expensive but current/specific) vs secondary (internal records, internet, government stats — cheap, fast, maybe outdated). Sampling: random, quota, stratified, convenience; bias risk with non-random.
  • Segmentation bases: age, income, gender, location, lifestyle, behaviour. Targeting & positioning basics.
  • Marketing mix (4Ps): Product (design, brand, packaging, life cycle: introduction→growth→maturity→decline with strategy at each stage, extension strategies) · Price (penetration, skimming, competition-based, cost-plus, psychological, promotional) · Promotion (advertising above/below the line, sales promotion, PR, personal selling, sponsorship; digital: social media, SEO) · Place (channels: direct, retailer, wholesaler, agent; e-commerce vs bricks).
  • Marketing budget, sales forecasting, ethics of promotion (truth in advertising, targeting children).

• Sources: internal (retained profits, sale of assets, owner's savings) vs external — short-term (overdraft, trade credit, invoice factoring) vs long-term (bank loan, mortgage, share issue, debentures, venture capital, microfinance). Match source to purpose (long asset = long source).
  • Cash flow ≠ profit (accruals, credit sales, capital spending). Forecast: opening + inflows − outflows = closing; improving cash flow: chase receivables, delay payables (carefully), reduce stock, overdraft facility, sale-and-leaseback.
  • Profit vs cash insolvency — profitable firms die of cash starvation.
  • Final accounts fluency: income statement → gross & net profit; SOFP layout; basic ratio reading (margin, ROCE, current ratio).
  • Break-even: contribution per unit (P − VC); BE output = FC ÷ contribution; margin of safety = actual − BE; target profit output = (FC + target) ÷ contribution; C/S ratio for multi-product; BE graph uses (assumptions: linear costs, constant price, single product).
  • Budgets: sales, production, purchases, labour, cash, master; variance = budget − actual (favourable/adverse); flexed budgets for realistic comparison.

• Organisation structures: tall (narrow span, many layers — close control, slow communication) vs flat (wide span — delegation, faster, risk of overload); matrix/project teams; delegation benefits & risks; centralisation vs decentralisation.
  • Recruitment & selection: job analysis → description & person specification → advertise → shortlist → interview/tests → appoint. Internal vs external recruitment trade-offs.
  • Training: induction, on-the-job (cheap, immediate, may pick up bad habits), off-the-job (expert input, cost, away from work). Development vs training.
  • Motivation theory: Taylor (money — piece rates; limits: ignores other needs), Mayo (social needs, teamwork, attention), Maslow (hierarchy: physiological → safety → social → esteem → self-actualisation), Herzberg (hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction: pay, conditions, policy; motivators create satisfaction: achievement, recognition, responsibility, advancement). Job enrichment vs enlargement.
  • Leadership styles: autocratic (crises, unskilled workers), democratic (motivation, slower), laissez-faire (experts), paternalistic; situational choice.
  • Communication: methods (meetings, email, notices), barriers (language, jargon, hierarchy, distance, emotion), grapevine.
  • Trade unions: collective bargaining, industrial action (strike, work-to-rule); employers' associations; ACAS-style conciliation/arbitration.

• Economies of scale: technical (specialisation, indivisibilities), managerial, financial (cheaper loans), marketing (bulk ads), risk-bearing — drive unit costs down as the firm grows; DISECONOMIES beyond optimum: communication breakdown, bureaucracy, alienation, slow decisions.
  • Quality: quality control (inspect at end — catch defects) vs quality assurance (standards at every stage — prevention culture, e.g. TQM, quality circles, benchmarking, ISO standards); cost of poor quality (returns, reputation).
  • Stock management: buffer stock, JIT (zero stock, reliable suppliers, frequent small deliveries — cuts storage cost, risk of production halts), stock turnover ratio.
  • Technology in production: CAD (design), CAM (manufacturing), CIM, robotics (consistency, 24/7, high setup cost), e-commerce.
  • External influences: government (taxation, minimum wage, health & safety, consumer protection, environmental law, subsidies), economic cycle (boom/recession effects on demand, employment), exchange rates (exporters/importers), competition, social trends, technology, legal, environmental (PESTLE recap).
  • Business ethics & stakeholders vs shareholders: triple bottom line (profit, people, planet).

• Paper 2 = case study + questions (2/4/6/8–12 marks). Levels of response: Knowledge → Application (case facts, $ figures, names) → Analysis (because → this means → therefore chains) → Evaluation (two sides + verdict).
  • The application habit: quote the case business's name, product, and numbers in every paragraph — it is the cheapest mark upgrade in Business.
  • Evaluate questions: conclusion compulsory (~half marks cap without one). Verdict formula: 'I recommend X because [case-linked reason], although [acknowledged trade-off].'
  • Time: 1.7 min/mark; the 12-marker gets ~20 minutes — plan for 3 minutes before writing.
  • MCQ: read for 'BEST' (most appropriate) wording; elimination beats guessing.

olevel/pak2059.b:
• 1857 War of Independence: causes — political (Doctrine of Lapse, annexations), economic (drain of wealth, land revenue destruction of artisans), religious (missionary activity, 1850 conversion law), military (general service enlistment, cartridge grievance). Failure: no central leadership, limited spread, no unified plan. Consequences: Mughal rule ends, Crown rule (1858 Government of India Act), Muslims scapegoated & excluded from jobs/education → later political awakening.
  • Sir Syed & the Aligarh Movement: loyal to the Crown post-1857; scientific English education for Muslims (MAO College 1875 → Aligarh Muslim University 1920); 1867 Hindi–Urdu controversy pushed him toward Muslim identity politics; Two-Nation thinking emerges.
  • 1906 Muslim League: Simla Deputation (loyalty + separate electorates) under Aga Khan & Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka; founded December 1906 — safeguard Muslim political rights. Separate electorates granted 1909 (Morley–Minto).
  • 1913–1916: League–Congress Lucknow Pact 1916 — Congress accepted separate electorates; Hindu–Muslim unity at its peak.
