• Khilafat Movement (1919–24): protect the Ottoman Caliph after WWI; Gandhi's support brought mass Muslim participation in Congress; ended abruptly when Ataturk abolished the Caliphate — Muslims felt betrayed by both Turkey & Congress.
  • Nehru Report (1928) rejected Muslim demands (separate electorates, 1/3 seats, provincial autonomy safeguards) → Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929) became the Muslim political charter: federation, provincial autonomy, separate electorates, one-third central seats, protection of culture & language.
  • Iqbal's Allahabad Address (1930): first demand for a separate Muslim state in the North-West — philosophical foundation.
  • Round Table Conferences (1930–32): failed — Congress rejected minority safeguards; Jinnah disillusioned, temporarily withdrew to London practice.
  • 1937 provincial elections & Congress rule (1937–39): League won few seats but claimed to represent all Muslims; Congress ministries' policies (Vidya Mandir, Wardha scheme, Bande Mataram, Hindi-Urdu tensions) convinced Muslims of Hindu majoritarian intent — the decisive radicaliser.
  • Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution, 23 March 1940, Minto Park: moved by A.K. Fazlul Haq — no constitutional plan acceptable without 'geographical contiguous units' for Muslims; did NOT use the word 'Pakistan' (Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet 1933 coined it) but demanded independent states.

• Cripps Mission (1942): dominion after the war with provinces opting out — Congress rejected; Quit India Movement followed.
  • Gandhi–Jinnah talks (1944): C.R. Formula for a Pakistan after the war if accepted — failed on timing & grouping.
  • Simla Conference (1945): failed on the Muslim League's claim to nominate all Muslims.
  • 1945–46 elections: League won ~90% of Muslim seats — sole representative claim confirmed.
  • Cabinet Mission Plan (1946): three-tier federation with groups A (Hindu majority), B & C (Muslim majority), centre limited to defence/foreign/communications — accepted by League, wrecked by Congress's interpretation; Interim Government formed (Nehru PM); League joined then resigned.
  • Direct Action Day (16 August 1946): Calcutta killings; communal violence spread. Interim government paralysis.
  • 3 June 1947 Plan & Mountbatten: partition with Bengal & Punjab referendums/assemblies; Radcliffe Boundary Award (published after independence — grievance source); 14 August 1947 — independence.

• Early problems: mass refugee settlement, canal water dispute (India cut water April 1948 — resolved via Inter-Dominion Agreement), division of assets & armed forces, Kashmir war (1947–48 — UNCIP ceasefire line, 1/3 of Kashmir with Pakistan), assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan (1951), provincial discord (Bengali vs West Pakistani), capital move Karachi → Islamabad (planned 1960s).
  • Constitutional delays: Objectives Resolution (1949 — Islamic provisions + democracy + minorities' rights); first constitution promulgated 23 March 1956 — parliamentary, Islamic Republic of Pakistan; abrogated 1958.
  • Economy: food shortages, jute/cotton export dependence, development programmes (Five-Year Plans from 1955), land reforms debate.

• Ayub Khan (1958–69): 1962 constitution — presidential, Basic Democracies (80,000 elected 'BD members' as electoral college), growth era (Green Revolution, Indus Waters Treaty 1960, Mangla/Tarbela dams, Pakistan's industrial takeoff) BUT inequality ('22 families'), no political freedom, 1965 war (Operation Gibraltar → Indian retaliation → Tashkent Agreement 1966), 1968–69 mass uprising → resignation.
  • Yahya Khan (1969–71): LFO 1970 — one-man-one-vote; 1970 elections: Mujib's Awami League swept East Pakistan (160 seats), Bhutto's PPP won West; power-transfer deadlock → Operation Searchlight (25 March 1971) → Liberation War → Indian intervention → 16 December 1971, Bangladesh.
  • Bhutto (1971–77): 1973 Constitution (parliamentary, federal, Islamic provisions, still current), Simla Agreement (1972), nuclear programme initiated, nationalisation of heavy industry/banks/education, labour reforms; allegations of rigging → PNA movement → Zia's coup (5 July 1977), Bhutto executed 1979.
  • Zia (1977–88): Islamisation (Hudood Ordinances 1979, zakat/usher 1980, interest-free banking steps, Shariat benches), Afghan jihad & Western aid (1980s), 8th Amendment (1985 — presidential powers, Article 58(2)(b)); died in air crash August 1988.

olevel/pak2059.t: P1 History — 6. 1988 to present & foreign policy
olevel/pak2059.b:
• 1988–99 democratic alternation: Benazir (1988–90, 1993–96) & Nawaz Sharif (1990–93, 1997–99) — instability, 8th vs 13th Amendments; 1998 nuclear tests (Chagai) after India's; Kargil 1999.
  • Musharraf (1999–2008): post-9/11 US alliance (war on terror), 17th Amendment, NRO, lawyers' movement; 2007 emergency; return to democracy 2008: 18th Amendment (2010) — parliamentary supremacy restored, provinces empowered (7th NFC Award), renaming NWFP → Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

olevel/pak2059.t: P1 History — 7. Society & culture (new syllabus topic)
olevel/pak2059.b:
• Languages: Urdu — national language, lingua franca, born in the subcontinent army camps; Punjabi (most spoken), Sindhi (Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai's poetry), Pashto (Khushal Khan Khattak), Balochi, Saraiki, Hindko, Brahui; regional language movements (Bengali Language Movement 1948–52 — seeds of separation; Sindhi-Urdu tensions 1972).
  • Religion & minorities: ~96% Muslim (Sunni majority; Shia, Ahmadi, Ismaili, Bohra communities); Christians, Hindus, Parsis, Sikhs — constitutional protection (Objective Resolution wording, reserved seats discussion, forced conversion debates).
  • Education: madrassa tradition (Deobandi/Barelvi/Ahl-i Hadith), Aligarh legacy, modern universities; literacy campaigns; Single National Curriculum debate.
  • Arts & media: truck art, miniature painting revival, classical music (Ustad Amanat Ali, Roshan Ara), qawwali (Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan), drama & film Lollywood→revival, television PTV era vs private channels/satellite.
  • Sports: hockey (Olympic golds 1960–84, World Cups), cricket (1992 World Cup, 2009 T20, 2017 Champions Trophy, Babar Azam era), squash (Jahangir Khan's 555-match streak), kabaddi.
  • Women: Fatima Jinnah, Begum Rana Liaquat (APWA), Benazir Bhutto (first woman PM of a Muslim-majority state), Malala Yousafzai (Nobel 2014); rights debates in law & practice.

• Location: 24°N–37°N, 61°E–77°E; borders — India (east, 3,323 km), Afghanistan (west/northwest, Durand Line 2,640 km), Iran (southwest, 909 km), China (northeast, 585 km, highest border Khunjerab 4,693 m). Arabian Sea coastline ~1,046 km (Sindh & Balochistan).
  • Plate tectonics: Indian plate colliding with Eurasian plate → the northern mountain wall still rising ~5 mm/year; earthquakes (2005 Kashmir, 2010 Balochistan) & landslides (Attabad 2010).
  • Regions north→south: Northern Mountains (Karakoram — K2 8,611 m, second highest on Earth; Himalaya — Nanga Parbat; Hindu Kush), Western Highlands (Sulaiman, Kirthar ranges — Sibi trough), Potohar Plateau & Salt Range (oil, coal, Khewra salt mine), Upper Indus Plain, Thar Desert (southeast), Lower Indus Plain, Balochistan Plateaus (insufficient rain — karez irrigation), Coastal areas (Indus delta, Karachi).
  • Indus River system: Indus + 5 tributaries — Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. Sources in Tibet/India; enters Pakistan near Attock. Indus Waters Treaty 1960 (World Bank): EASTERN rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) → India; WESTERN rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) → Pakistan, with 10-year transition financing.

olevel/pak2059.t: P2 Environment — 2. Climate, hazards & climate change
olevel/pak2059.b:
• Climate controls: continental interior (extremes of temperature), latitude, altitude, monsoon, distance from sea.
  • Monsoon (July–September): pressure reversal — intense summer heat over land → low pressure → moist SW winds from the Bay of Bengal → Himalayas force uplift → 60–70% of annual rain. Western depressions (December–March) bring rain to the north/west. Tropical cyclones (Arabian Sea, May–June & October–November) hit Sindh coast (Karachi 2021).
  • Regional pattern: arid Balochistan/Sindh (<250 mm), semi-arid Punjab, humid north; snowfall above ~1,500 m.
  • Hazards: floods (2010: 20% of the country inundated; 2022 super-floods from monster monsoon + glacier melt), droughts (Thar, Cholistan — recurring famine cycles), earthquakes (2005: 80,000+ deaths), GLOF (glacial lake outburst floods in Gilgit-Baltistan), heatwaves (Jacobabad, Karachi 2015), sea intrusion in Indus delta (1.2 million acres lost since the 1950s).
  • Climate change (new syllabus focus): Pakistan emits <1% of global GHG yet is top-10 most affected; melting Hindu Kush-Karakoram-Himalaya glaciers ('Third Pole' — 7,000+ glaciers) threaten long-term water security; responses — mitigation (Billion Tree Tsunami/10 Billion Tree Tsunami reforestation, 60% renewable energy target 2030, coal phase-down debate) & adaptation (early warning systems, GLOF monitoring with UNDP, heat action plans Karachi, resilient crops, water pricing).

• ~240 million (2023 census, 5th most populous); growth rate ~1.6–2%; TFR declining (~3.3); youthful pyramid (median age ~20); density highest in Punjab; 2023 census controversy (Sindh objections, digital count debates).
  • Migration: rural→urban push (land fragmentation, unemployment, services) pull (jobs, education, healthcare); 3–4 million Afghan refugees (largest protracted refugee population; repatriation waves); Gulf emigration (remittances ~$30bn/year — economic lifeline); internal: Karachi receives ~1 million migrants/decade.
  • Urbanisation: Karachi (~17–20 million — financial capital, port, problems: water (1050 MGD demand vs 600 supply), katchi abadis (Orangi Town — world's largest informal settlement, Orangi Pilot Project success), sanitation (Lyari & Malir rivers as sewers), transport (no mass transit until Green Line 2022), pollution, crime cycles). Lahore (~13 million), Faisalabad (Manchester of Pakistan — textiles), Islamabad-Rawalpindi twin city (planned capital, highest HDI), Peshawar, Quetta, Multan, Hyderabad.
  • Responses: katchi abadi upgrading (Khuda Ki Basti model — Hyderabad: land title + services at affordable rates), Master Plans (Karachi 2030 weakly enforced), new cities debate (Ravi Riverfront, Gwadar), devolution under 18th Amendment (local governments weakly empowered).
  • Quality of life: HDI ~0.54 (medium-low); literacy ~58% (female ~49%); health indicators improving (life expectancy ~66; infant mortality ~52/1000); Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP — cash transfers to 9 million families), Sehat Sahulat health cards; poverty ~24% (multidimensional higher).

• Agriculture: ~19% of GDP, ~37% of employment, ~60–70% of export earnings indirectly. Subsistence + commercial mix; average farm size shrinking (fragmentation through inheritance).
  • Crops: cotton (lint — textile backbone; Punjab + Sindh; pests: pink bollworm; BT cotton debate), wheat (staple; Rabi), rice (Basmati — premium export; Kharif), sugarcane (Punjab's water-hungry giant; mill-politics), maize (fast-growing), fruits (mangoes — Chaunsa, Sindhri; kinnow; dates from Balochistan), vegetables.
  • Livestock: ~60% of agricultural value — cattle, buffalo (milk: world's 3rd/4th largest producer), goats (beetal), poultry (fastest-growing subsector); hides → leather exports.
  • Fishing: Karachi (majority of the catch), Gwadar, Pasni; Indus delta shrimp; potential largely unexploited (deep-sea fleet small).
  • Forestry: ~5% forest cover (target 25% by policy — far off); coniferous north (pine, deodar — timber, paper), riverine forests (Sindh), mangroves (Indus delta — world's 5th largest, protects coast, carbon sink, threatened by sea intrusion & fuelwood).
  • Minerals: coal (Thar — one of the world's largest lignite reserves, being mined for power; Sindh's game-changer), natural gas (Sui — declining; LNG imports now), oil (limited, Attock/Upper Sindh), chromite, gypsum, limestone, marble (Gilgit-Baltistan & KP gem belt: emerald, ruby, topaz), uranium (Dera Ghazi Khan), salt (Khewra).
  • Irrigation: world's largest contiguous irrigation system — 3 storage dams (Tarbela, Mangla, Warsak), 19 barrages, 12 link canals, 40,000+ miles of canals; tubewells (3 million+, falling water tables in Punjab); karez in Balochistan; waterlogging & salinity (SCARP tubewells to drain); efficiency: ~40% (losses to seepage/evaporation — lining debate).

olevel/pak2059.t: P2 Environment — 5. Economy: industry, energy, trade & development
olevel/pak2059.b:
• Industry: textiles = ~60% of exports (spinning/weaving concentrated Faisalabad, Karachi, Lahore; vertical integration incomplete — low value-added share), food processing (sugar, flour, rice mills), cement (Maple Leaf, Lucky — capacity > demand; Afghan export market), fertiliser (Engro, FFC — gas-based), automobiles (assemblers: Pak Suzuki, Toyota Indus, Honda; EV policy new), steel (Pakistan Steel Mills — loss-making debate), pharmaceuticals (sufficient generics), sports goods (Sialkot — ~70% of world hand-stitched footballs), surgical instruments (Sialkot — world-class), leather, carpets, IT exports (fastest-growing, ~$2.6bn target).
  • Energy: chronic crisis — demand > supply; circular debt (~2.4 trillion PKR) cripples the chain; mix: gas (38%, declining), oil (25%, imported), hydel (27%, seasonal), coal (Thar expanding), nuclear (K-2/K-3 Karachi 2,200 MW; Chashma plants), solar/wind growing (Quaid-e-Azam Solar Park Bahawalpur 1,000 MW; Jhimpir wind corridor). CPEC energy projects added ~5,000+ MW (coal-heavy: Sahiwal, Port Qasim, Hub). Line losses & theft ~15%.
  • Trade: exports ($30–35bn: textiles, rice, leather, sports goods, surgical instruments) vs imports ($70–80bn: petroleum, machinery, edible oil, tea, pulses) → chronic trade deficit; remittances (~$30bn, 2nd biggest FX source after exports); major partners: USA, China, UAE, EU (GSP+ since 2014 — textile duty advantage), Saudi Arabia.
  • Services & tourism: finance (Karachi Stock Exchange merged PSX), telecoms (huge mobile penetration), transport (NHA motorways: M-2 Lahore–Islamabad; CPEC western route developing); tourism potential: northern areas (Hunza, Skardu, Swat — Lonely Planet top region 2020), religious tourism (Nankana Sahib for Sikhs), coastal (Gwadar, Ormara) — held back by security perception & infrastructure.
  • Development strategy: CPEC ($60bn+ corridor: energy, motorways, Gwadar port & airport, SEZs) — opportunities (infrastructure, jobs, industrialisation) vs concerns (debt load, transparency, regional imbalance — Baloch grievances).

olevel/pak2059.t: P2 Environment — 6. Exam technique & data skills
olevel/pak2059.b:
• Resource-based questions: read the resource FIRST, then the questions; quote resource figures in answers ('the map shows rainfall below 250 mm in Balochistan, so…').
  • NEW format decision-making part: weigh ≥2 options with resource evidence, give a COMMITTED recommendation with reasons — never sit on the fence.
  • Map skills: 4- and 6-figure grid references, direction (three-figure bearing), scale distance, contour reading (relief & rivers), identifying features (settlements on valley floors — water/flat land).
  • Data skills: bar/line/pie reading, % change calculation, population pyramids (wide base = youthful → schools needed; narrow top = low life expectancy), climate graphs (temperature + rainfall together — tropical monsoon pattern: hot wet summer, cool dry winter).
  • Case-study answers need named places + figures: 'Karachi's population of ~17 million with 1050 MGD water demand vs 600 MGD supply' beats 'Karachi has water problems' every time.
  • Essay plans (P1): intro with dates & thesis → 3 argued factors (with evidence) → counter-perspective → committed verdict ('on balance… because…').

alevel/m9709.b:
• Quadratics: discriminant conditions, completing the square for vertex form, roots relations S = −b/a, P = c/a; solve inequalities with the parabola's shape (sketch first).
  • Functions: domain/range, composite fg (inside first), inverse f⁻¹, transformations y = f(x)+a, y = f(x+a), y = af(x), y = f(ax) — know each's effect cold.
  • Coordinate geometry: line equations, parallel/perpendicular conditions, midpoints, distances; circle (x−a)² + (y−b)² = r² and the expanded form.
  • Circular measure: radians (π rad = 180°), s = rθ, A = ½r²θ — sectors, segments, arc problems.
  • Trigonometry: identities (sin²+cos² = 1, tan = sin/cos), solving equations with general solutions (nπ ± α for sin, 2nπ ± α for cos, nπ + α for tan); R-formula a cosθ + b sinθ = R cos(θ − α).
  • Differentiation from first principles; chain/product/quotient; stationary points classified; integration as reverse; definite integrals = areas (areas BELOW axis give negative — split!); volumes of revolution.

• Algebra: modulus |x|, solving |f(x)| = g(x) by squaring or case split; polynomials — factor/remainder theorem, solving cubics; partial fractions (distinct, repeated, quadratic factors).
  • Logs & exponentials: ln x and e^x, solving a^x = b via logs, growth/decay models (population, cooling, compound interest continuous).
  • Trigonometry: sec/cosec/cot, identities 1 + tan² = sec², solving harder equations in given ranges; harmonic form for max/min problems.
  • Differentiation: implicit, parametric (dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)), d²y/dx² for parametric (divide by dx/dt again); connected rates of change.
  • Integration: substitution (choose u = inner function), parts (∫u dv = uv − ∫v du, LIATE), improper integrals with limits; differential equations — separate variables then apply initial conditions; exponential growth solutions N = N₀e^(kt).
  • Vectors: 3D lines r = a + λb; shortest distance from point to line; intersection of lines; scalar product for angles (cos θ = a·b/|a||b|) and perpendicularity.

• Forces & equilibrium: resolving, triangle of forces, friction F ≤ μR (limiting at equality), inclined planes (split weight into mg sinθ ∥, mg cosθ ⊥).
  • Kinematics: SUVAT extended with calculus (v = ds/dt, a = dv/dt, s = ∫v dt); motion graphs; multi-stage journeys.
  • Newton's 2nd law: F = ma as a vector equation; connected particles (pulleys, lifts — apparent weight), momentum & impulse, conservation of momentum in 1D collisions (direct impact, Newton's law of restitution e = speed of separation/speed of approach for A2 extension).
  • Work, energy, power: work–energy theorem, GPE/KE exchange with friction losses; power P = Fv (max speed when P = resistance × v — the car-top-speed classic).

• Permutations & combinations: nPr, nCr; arrangements with repeats n!/(a!b!); selection problems (at least one = complement).
  • Probability: conditional P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B); independence test P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B); tree & Venn methods.
  • Discrete random variables: E(X) = Σxp, Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]²; Binomial B(n,p): P(X=r) = C(n,r)p^r q^(n−r), mean np, variance npq; Geometric distribution.
  • Continuous RV: pdf f(x) — total area 1, P(a
  • Normal distribution: z = (X−μ)/σ; use of tables; normal approximation to binomial (np > 5, nq > 5 with continuity correction); sum of normal variables stays normal.

• ~11 structured questions escalating in demand; later parts use earlier answers (error carried forward) — NEVER abandon a part.
  • Method marks dominate: correct set-up (integral, equation) earns most marks even with arithmetic slips.
  • Trig answers: general solution unless a range is given; degrees vs radians — the paper specifies; mixing them is the classic mark killer.
  • Stats: define the distribution ('Let X ~ B(20, 0.3)'), state the test, show the calculation, interpret in context ('P(X ≥ 12) = 0.0213 < 0.05, so reject H₀').
  • Mechanics: draw the diagram, mark forces, define the positive direction BEFORE equations; answers with units (N, m/s, J).
  • Check questions demanding 'exact' answers (leave in π, e, ln, surds) vs 3 s.f.

alevel/ch9701.b:
• Enthalpy: Hess cycles, bond enthalpies (average, gas phase), calorimetry q = mcΔT with corrections; ionisation energy trends explained by nuclear charge/radius/shielding; electron affinity.
  • Kinetics: rate equations from initial-rates tables (orders, k with units), mechanisms (rate-determining step must match the rate equation), Arrhenius: ln k = ln A − Eₐ/RT (gradient of ln k vs 1/T = −Eₐ/R); Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution sketches with Eₐ and T changes; homogeneous vs heterogeneous catalysts.
  • Equilibrium: Kc & Kp with ICE tables (mol → concentration via V; partial pressures via mole fractions); units of K; effects of T/P/catalyst on position and on K (only T changes K); industrial contexts (Haber, Contact).

• Redox: oxidation states & balancing; standard electrode potentials E°; cell emf = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); ΔG = −nFE; feasibility (E° > +0.3 V likely; < −0.3 V not); Nernst idea (concentration effects).
  • Electrolysis: products at each electrode (discharge series), quantities Q = It, moles = Q/nF; electroplating/refining calculations.
  • Acids & bases: Brønsted theory, Kw, pH of strong/weak acids (weak needs Ka and an ICE table), buffers (Henderson–Hasselbalch pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid])) and how they resist added acid/base; titration curves (indicators chosen by pH range) and curve shapes for all four acid/base strength combos.

• Group 2: reactivity ↑ down (ionisation energy argument), reactions with water/oxygen/acids, solubility trends of hydroxides (↑ down) and sulfates (↓ down) explained by lattice vs hydration enthalpies; flame tests & uses (Mg in alloys, Ca in bones/plaster, BaSO₄ in X-ray 'barium meals').
  • Group 17: oxidising power ↓ down (attraction for incoming electron), displacement reactions, reactions with NaOH (cold dilute → chlorate(I); hot concentrated → chlorate(V)) as disproportionation; halide tests (AgNO₃/HNO₃ colours).
  • Transition metals: d-block configurations (3d & 4s), definition criteria (ions with partially filled d-subshell), variable oxidation states (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cu⁺/Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺…MnO₄⁻), COLOURED ions from d-electron transitions (energy gap ΔE = hν; colour absorbed vs observed complementary), catalysts (Fe/Haber, V₂O₅/Contact, Ni/hydrogenation, Pd/Pt hydrogenation), complex ions & ligand exchange (Cu(H₂O)₆²⁺ blue → CuCl₄²⁻ yellow-green; NH₃ stepwise to deep-blue tetraammine), bi-dentate ligands & EDTA; haemoglobin & cisplatin as applied examples.

• Naming & isomerism: IUPAC names, structural/displayed formulae, E/Z with CIP priority rules, optical isomers (chiral centres, plane-polarised light).
  • Mechanisms with curly arrows FROM electron pairs: nucleophilic substitution (SN1 tertiary, SN2 primary — know both routes), electrophilic addition (alkene + Br₂/HBr — Markovnikov via carbocation stability), free-radical substitution (alkanes — initiation/propagation/termination), nucleophilic addition to carbonyls (CN⁻ then H⁺ → hydroxynitrile), condensation/esterification, electrophilic substitution of benzene (Br₂/FeBr₃, HNO₃/H₂SO₄ nitration, Friedel–Crafts alkylation/acylation) — delocalised π system attacks the electrophile.
  • Synthesis routes: learn the connectivity — alcohol ⇌ alkene → dihalo → dialcohol; oxidation ladders (primary alcohol → aldehyde → acid); nitrile route to amines & carboxylic acids; benzene → phenylamine via nitration/reduction.
  • Analysis: IR (O–H broad 3230–3550, C=O ~1700, fingerprint), mass spec (molecular ion = M; fragments), ¹H NMR (chemical shift tables, integration, n+1 splitting, D₂O exchange for –OH), ¹³C NMR (number of environments); combine all three to identify unknowns.

• P2 (AS): short structured — definitions word-perfect, calculations show working (Kc answers to 3 s.f. with units), organic mechanisms with correct curly-arrow direction.
  • P4 (A2): longer structured — expect multi-step synthesis with reasons ('why is the yield low' → side reactions, volatility, transfer losses), thermodynamics cycles, Born–Haber style reasoning.
  • P5: design experiments — identify variables, sketch the graph treatment (e.g., plot log rate vs log concentration → gradient = order), error analysis (systematic vs random, % uncertainty = uncertainty/measurement × 100).
  • Definitions bank: activation energy, homolytic vs heterolytic fission, electrophile/nucleophile, standard cell potential, buffer, ligand, dative bond, stereoisomerism.
  • Always state assumptions (e.g., 'assuming the acid is monoprotic', 'gas behaves ideally').

alevel/ph9702.b:
• Kinematics & dynamics with calculus; projectiles; equilibrium with vector resolution; moments & centre of gravity.
  • Momentum, impulse & collisions; work, energy, power (P = Fv); efficiency.
  • Matter: density, pressure, upthrust (Archimedes), fluid flow; kinetic theory deriving pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩; r.m.s. speed ∝ √(T/M); Brownian motion evidence.
  • Elastic properties: Hooke, Young modulus E = stress/strain, energy stored = ½FΔx; force–extension and stress–strain graphs for brittle/ductile/polymeric materials.

• Gravitation: F = GMm/r², field g = GM/r², potential φ = −GM/r, orbital mechanics v = √(GM/r), T² ∝ r³ (Kepler); geostationary satellites (T = 24 h above equator, r ≈ 42 400 km).
  • Electric: F = kQ₁Q₂/r², E = kQ/r² (radial), V = kQ/r; uniform fields E = V/d; capacitors C = εA/d, Q = CV, energy ½CV²; series/parallel; RC discharge V = V₀e^(−t/RC), τ = RC, ln V–t graphs for half-life analogues.
  • Magnetic: F = BIL sinθ, F = Bqv; circular motion of charges r = mv/qB; velocity selector; Hall voltage; magnetic flux Φ = BA, Faraday's law ε = −N dΦ/dt, Lenz's law; transformers & the grid (E = I²R argument for high-V transmission).

• SHM: a = −ω²x, T = 2π√(m/k) = 2π√(L/g); energy interchange; resonance & damping (light/heavy/critical).
  • Waves: superposition, interference (path difference nλ vs (n+½)λ), diffraction grating d sinθ = nλ, stationary waves in pipes/strings; Doppler effect f′ = fv/(v ± v_s); ultrasound medical imaging.
  • Thermal: first law ΔU = q + w; specific/latent experiments; ideal gas pV = nRT, kinetic theory links; black-body radiation & Wien's law (A2).
  • Modern: photoelectric effect E = hf − φ (stopping potential, threshold frequency — particle nature of light); de Broglie λ = h/p; energy levels & line spectra (Bohr); absorption/emission spectra uses in astronomy; radioactive decay N = N₀e^(−λt), t½ = ln2/λ, dating; binding energy curve & E = mc²; fission/fission reactors (moderator, control rods, coolant, critical mass); Hubble & the expanding universe (A2).

• X-rays: production (bremsstrahlung & characteristic), attenuation I = I₀e^(−μx), contrast media, CT scanning vs conventional radiography.
  • Ultrasound: pulse-echo A/B scans, acoustic impedance Z = ρc, Doppler blood-flow.
  • MRI: strong field aligns protons, RF pulses, relaxation signals — superb soft tissue, no ionising radiation.
  • PET: positron annihilation γ detection; tracers & gamma cameras.
  • Lasers & fibre optics in medicine/endoscopy.

• Definitions word-perfect ('the rate of change of momentum', 'work done per unit charge'); explain = mechanism chains.
  • Diagrams: field lines, circuits, ray diagrams labelled; graphs with labelled axes and quantified intercepts.
  • Calculations: formula → rearrange → substitute with units → answer 2–3 s.f.; powers-of-ten discipline with prefixes.
  • P5 experiment design: variables stated, procedure enabling repeats, graph manipulation to linearise (e.g., plot T² vs m → gradient 4π²/k).
  • Estimate questions: order-of-magnitude reasoning earns marks — always attempt.

alevel/bio9700.b:
• Ultrastructure from EM images; magnification calculations; cytoskeleton; endosymbiotic theory evidence (mitochondria/chloroplasts: double membranes, own DNA/ribosomes).
  • Membrane structure (fluid mosaic): phospholipid bilayer, proteins (carrier/channel/receptor/glycoprotein roles), cholesterol; factors on diffusion/osmosis/active transport rates; facilitated diffusion vs active transport (ATP, against gradient).
  • Cell division: mitosis stages & significance (growth/repair/asexual), meiosis & variation; stem cells (totipotent → pluripotent), therapeutic cloning debate.
  • Enzymes deep: Vmax & Km from Michaelis–Menten, competitive vs non-competitive inhibition (Km shifts), immobilised enzymes (industry: pectinase in juice, lactase in milk).

• Water & hydrogen bonding in biology; carbohydrates (mono/di/polysaccharides: α-glucose vs β-glucose — cellulose straight chains vs starch amylose helix); proteins (primary→quaternary, R-groups, denaturation); lipids (triglycerides, phospholipids, test emulsions).
  • DNA: structure (Watson–Crick), base pairing, replication semi-conservative (Meselson–Stahl), protein synthesis outline: transcription (nucleus) → mRNA → translation at ribosomes (codons/anticodons); mutations & consequences (sickle cell as case).
  • Gas transport: haemoglobin loading/unloading curves, Bohr shift, fetal haemoglobin; carbonic anhydrase & the chloride shift.
  • Heart & ECG; xylem transport (cohesion–tension, root pressure, capillarity), transpiration factors (humidity/wind/light/temperature experiments with potometer); phloem mass flow (source → sink, bidirectional evidence from aphid stylets & ringing).
  • Immunity: phagocytosis, clonal selection of lymphocytes, antibodies (structure & agglutination), vaccination & herd immunity; HIV lifecycle & immunosuppression.

• Respiration: glycolysis (cytoplasm, net 2 ATP, 2 NADH) → link reaction → Krebs cycle (CO₂, NADH, FADH₂, 1 ATP) → oxidative phosphorylation (ETC + chemiosmosis in cristae; ~28–30 ATP total); anaerobic in mammals vs yeast; respiratory substrates compared (carbohydrate vs lipid RQ).
  • Photosynthesis: light-dependent stage (thylakoids: photoactivation of PSII, photolysis of water, electron transport → chemiosmosis → ATP & reduced NADP) and Calvin cycle (stroma: CO₂ fixation by RuBP/rubisco → GP → TP using ATP & reduced NADP; TP → glucose or regenerate RuBP); limiting factors experiments (algal balls, pondweed, oxygen electrode); C4 & CAM as adaptations (A2 context).
  • Both processes compared: membranes as energy-transducing systems; ATP the universal currency.

• Nervous control: resting/action potentials (sodium–potassium pump, voltage-gated channels), saltatory conduction, synapse transmission (Ca²⁺, neurotransmitter, receptors); drug action at synapses (nicotine, MDMA).
  • Homeostasis: thermoregulation, blood glucose (insulin/glucagon second-messenger mechanism), kidney & ADH/osmoregulation; liver as homeostatic hub.
  • Plant hormones: auxins & phototropism/gravitropism (differential elongation), gibberellins & stem elongation/dormancy, ethene ripening, abscisic acid stomatal control; commercial applications.
  • Genetics: test crosses, codominance & multiple alleles (ABO), sex linkage (colour blindness, haemophilia), autosomal linkage & cross-over values, epistasis ratios (9:3:3:1 variants), chi-squared tests; Hardy–Weinberg p² + 2pq + q² = 1 & selection calculations; speciation (allopatric vs sympatric), selection types (stabilising/directional/disruptive); artificial selection & GMOs (vector plasmids, restriction enzymes, ligase, marker genes); PCR & gel electrophoresis; gene therapy & screening ethics.
  • Ecosystems: energy flow & ecological pyramids, nutrient cycles (carbon, nitrogen), succession, conservation management, populations & limiting factors (sigmoid growth, r vs K strategists).

• Data questions dominate: quote numbers from the graph/table in your explanation ('as CO₂ rises from 0.03% to 0.1%, rate rises from 10 to 22 bubbles/min, because…').
  • 'Explain' chains: mechanism with because/therefore; link structure → function every time.
  • P3 practical: familiarise with microscope measuring (eyepiece graticule calibration), drawings (plan & detail rules), enzyme/kinetics/photosynthesis standard experiments.
  • P5: chi-squared (state H₀, expected from ratio, Σ(O−E)²/E, compare to critical value at p = 0.05, conclude); design questions — control variables ×3, repeats & mean, named statistical test with justification.
  • Definitions: diffusion/osmosis/active transport (word-perfect), photosynthesis, respiration, homeostasis, negative feedback, transpiration, gene/allele/locus.

alevel/acc9706.b:
• Double-entry mastery assumed from O Level; focus on errors, suspense, and control accounts with complex adjustments (contra, refunds, dishonoured cheques, interest on overdue accounts).
  • Partnerships: capital vs current accounts, appropriation statement, goodwill on admission/retirement/death (revaluation account method), loans from partners (interest = expense).
  • Companies: bonus & rights issues (share premium movements), debentures vs shares (interest vs dividend; tax treatment), dividends (interim/final/proposed), reserves & their uses, bonus issue from share premium ONLY.
  • Incomplete records: control-account & 'total' methods, cash summaries, markup/margin conversions, statement of affairs.
  • Manufacturing accounts: prime cost → factory overheads (under/over-absorption) → cost of production; income statement presentation for a manufacturer.

• Ratio suite with formulas & verdicts: profitability (gross margin, operating margin, ROCE, ROE), liquidity (current, acid test, cash flow), efficiency (asset turnover, inventory days, receivables days, payables days — the working-capital cycle), gearing (debt/equity, interest cover), investment (EPS, dividend yield, P/E).
  • Trend + comparative analysis ('gross margin fell from 32% to 27% — possibly discounting to clear inventory, supported by inventory days rising 45→68').
  • Limitations: inflation, one-off items, creative accounting, sector differences, seasonal trading.
  • Cash flow statements (IAS 7 indirect method): operating (profit + depreciation − gains ± working capital), investing, financing; reconciling profit to cash movement — the classic 'why profitable but no cash' answer.
  • Consolidated basics (if in syllabus year): goodwill, non-controlling interest, intra-group trading & unrealised profit.

• Cost classification & behaviour (fixed/stepped/variable/semi-variable with high-low method); overhead absorption: allocation → apportionment → reapportionment (reciprocal services) → absorption by OAR; under/over absorption explained & adjusted.
  • Marginal costing: contribution per unit/unit limiting factor; make-or-buy; special orders (relevant costing — ignore sunk costs & unavoidable fixed costs); break-even & margin of safety multi-product (C/S ratio).
  • Absorption vs marginal profit reconciliation (inventory change × fixed overhead per unit).
  • Process costing: normal loss (scrap value credit), abnormal loss/gain accounts, equivalent units for WIP; joint products vs by-products (split-off, NRV method).
  • Job/batch/service costing features.
  • Standard costing & variance analysis: material price/usage, labour rate/efficiency, variable overhead, fixed overhead expenditure/volume, sales price/volume; interdependence (favourable price + adverse usage = cheaper poorer material); basic variance investigation rules.
  • Budgeting: functional budgets → cash budget → master budget; flexed budgets for control; behavioural aspects (budgetary slack, participation).
  • Investment appraisal: NPV (discount tables, accept > 0), IRR (interpolation), payback & discounted payback, ARR; qualitative factors; sensitivity (which variable kills NPV first).

• P2 (90 marks, answer structured questions): formats earn presentation marks — ruled, headed, dated; workings columns for every calculated figure.
  • Own-figure rule everywhere: method marks survive arithmetic slips; never leave parts blank.
  • P3 (A2 structured): cash flow statement order memorised (operating → investing → financing); ratio questions demand COMPARISON + consequence.
  • P4 (Cost & Management): show formulas (contribution per unit, OAR, NPV layout); state assumptions; discount factors copied correctly.
  • MCQ: watch double negatives, 'which is NOT', and units (per unit vs total).

alevel/bus9609.b:
• Entrepreneurship & intrapreneurship; business planning (the living document); economic sectors & their shifts; stakeholders mapping & conflicting objectives (shareholders vs community vs environment).
  • Organisational design: tall/flat/matrix/entrepreneurial (Burns & Stalker contingency); delegation, span of control, centralisation; organisational culture (Handy's types) & cultural web.
  • HR planning: labour turnover formula & remedies; recruitment economics (costs of bad hire); selection validity (interviews' weaknesses — halo effect, structured alternatives: assessment centres, psychometrics, work sampling).
  • Motivation in depth: content theories (Maslow, Herzberg, McClelland's need for achievement) vs process theories (Vroom's expectancy: effort → performance → reward valence; Adams' equity; Locke's goal-setting SMART); financial motivators (piece rate, commission, profit-sharing, ESOPs, fringe benefits) vs non-financial (job rotation/enlargement/enrichment, empowerment, quality circles, flexible working, teamworking).
  • Leadership: style continua (Tannenbaum–Schmidt), contingency models (Fiedler: task vs relationship orientation matched to situation; Hersey–Blanchard readiness), transformational vs transactional (Bass), charismatic & its risks.
  • Communication: channels & richness, barriers, networks; conflict & change management (Kotter's 8 steps, Lewin's force-field).

• Marketing strategy: segmentation (bases & effective segmentation tests), targeting (undifferentiated/concentrated/differentiated), positioning maps; marketing planning & budgets; digital marketing metrics (click-through, conversion, cost-per-acquisition); relationship marketing & loyalty schemes.
  • Product decisions: Boston matrix (question marks→stars→cash cows→dogs strategies), product life cycle extension strategies, branding & packaging psychology, new product development stages.

  • Distribution: channel length decisions, vertical/horizontal integration, franchising, e-commerce disintermediation.
  • Operations: capacity utilisation & its economics; lean production (5S, kaizen, JIT, TQM — Deming, quality circles, benchmarking, Six Sigma overview); network analysis (CPA: earliest/latest start, float, crashing); R&D, patents; technology (CAD/CAM/CIM/AI/robotics) and its HR implications.
  • Inventory management beyond EOQ: JIT partnerships, safety stock maths; quality costs (prevention vs appraisal vs internal/external failure).

• Financial: cash-flow forecasting & remedies; working capital cycle & optimisation; budgets & variance; final accounts & ratio suite (as 9706 but applied to business decisions: 'should the bank extend the overdraft?'); sources of finance matched to need & gearing effects.
  • Strategic tools: mission/vision/objectives (SMART); SWOT & TOWS; PESTLE; Porter's Five Forces (industry attractiveness); Porter's generic strategies (cost leadership, differentiation, focus) & stuck-in-the-middle; Ansoff; Boston; core competence (Prahalad & Hamel); benchmarking; the value chain (primary vs support activities); synergy & the 7-S framework as integration checklists.
  • Growth: organic vs external (mergers: horizontal/vertical/conglomerate; takeovers; MBOs; joint ventures; strategic alliances); integration motives & failure rates (culture clash, overpayment, due diligence).
  • Globalisation vs localisation (glocalisation); market entry modes (export → licensing → franchising → JV → FDI); trading blocs & WTO; exchange-rate exposure (transaction/translation/economic) & hedging basics.
  • Ethics, CSR & ESG: Friedman vs Freeman (shareholder vs stakeholder); triple bottom line; Friedman: 'the social responsibility of business is to increase profits' (within rules) vs Porter & Kramer's 'shared value'; whistleblowing, governance codes.
  • Contingency planning, crisis management, business continuity.

• Levels of response: K → APPL (case facts) → AN (because/therefore chains) → EVAL (two sides + committed verdict). A 12-marker without conclusion caps ~6.
  • P1 (1 h 15, 40): Section A short questions test precise knowledge (formulas, theory names, examples) — answer crisply; Section B one question with 8 & 12 mark parts.
  • P2 (1 h 30, 60): data response — quote the case data (exhibits!) in every developed paragraph; calculation parts show working.
  • P3 (3 h, 100): the big one. Essay plans: define → apply framework → case evidence → counter-argument → verdict with numbers ('with $2m cash per Exhibit 3, diversification is affordable but…').
  • Memorise a template paragraph per strategy tool so the exam is assembly, not invention.
  • Timing discipline: 1.8 min/mark on P3 — plan 5 min/essay.

alevel/eco9708.b:
• Scarcity, choice, opportunity cost; PPF (points inside = unemployment, on = efficient, outside = unattainable; growth shifts it out).
  • Demand & supply: shifts vs movements; determinants; consumer & producer surplus; price elasticity PED = %ΔQd/%ΔP (determinants: substitutes, necessity, income share, time) with revenue-rule applications; PES; YED (normal/inferior); XED (substitutes/complements).
  • Intervention: maximum prices (shortages → queues/rationing/black markets) & minimum prices (surpluses → buffer stocks); indirect taxes (statutory vs economic incidence — falls heavier on inelastic side) & subsidies; PED determines effectiveness of 'sin taxes'.

• Market failure types: externalities (MSC vs MSB diagrams, welfare triangles), public goods (non-rival, non-excludable — free-rider), merit/demerit goods (information gaps), factor immobility (geographical/occupational), inequality, monopoly power.
  • Government responses: taxes/subsidies, regulation, permits (tradable pollution permits), state provision, information campaigns, nudges; government failure (imperfect information, unintended consequences, administrative costs, political cycles).
  • Costs & revenue: TC = TFC + TVC; AC, MC, AFC geometry; normal vs supernormal profit; profit max MR = MC.
  • Perfect competition: price-taker, MR = P, long-run normal profit, allocative & productive efficiency — the benchmark.
  • Monopoly: downward AR & MR, price > MC, deadweight loss, X-inefficiency, rent-seeking; natural monopoly; price discrimination (conditions, consumer surplus capture); regulation (price capping RPI−X, profit regulation, nationalisation vs privatisation).
  • Monopolistic competition & oligopoly: kinked demand (price rigidity), game theory (prisoner's dilemma, Nash, collusion vs competition — cartels & their instability), contestable markets (Baumol — threat of entry disciplines).
  • Monopsony (single buyer: NHS as labour monopsonist — minimum wage can raise BOTH wages and employment, the diagram worth memorising).
  • Labour market: MRP theory, demand for labour = MRP; supply determinants; wage differentials (MRP vs non-pecuniary factors); transfer earnings vs economic rent.

• National income: GDP/GNP/NNP, real vs nominal (GDP deflator), per capita & its limits (HDI alternative); circular flow (injections J = I + G + X, withdrawals W = S + T + M; equilibrium Y when J = W).
  • AD/AS: AD components C+I+G+(X−M); SRAS shapes (Keynesian horizontal→vertical, classical vertical); shifts & macro outcomes (growth, demand-pull vs cost-push inflation, deflationary gaps).
  • Inflation: CPI measurement, causes (demand-pull, cost-push, monetary, imported), consequences (menu/shoe-leather, redistribution, uncertainty, competitiveness) & anti-inflation policy trade-offs (Phillips short-run; expectations-augmented long-run vertical at NRU — Friedman & Phelps).
  • Unemployment: types (frictional, structural, cyclical/demand-deficient, seasonal, technological, voluntary) & costs (lost output Okun, fiscal cost, social); policies targeted per type.
  • Balance of payments: current account components (trade in goods/services, primary & secondary income); causes of deficits (competitiveness, growth differentials, structural); corrections (expenditure-reducing: deflation; expenditure-switching: devaluation — Marshall–Lerner PEDx + PEDm > 1 & the J-curve; supply-side).
  • Exchange rates: floating determination, fixed/managed systems; appreciation vs depreciation effects (BOP, inflation, growth); currency unions criteria (optimum currency area).

• Fiscal policy: budget stances, automatic stabilisers vs discretionary; multiplier k = 1/(MPS+MPT+MPM) & its limitations (crowding out, supply constraints, expectations/ricardian equivalence); public debt sustainability; Laffer curve (tax rate vs revenue).
  • Monetary policy: interest-rate transmission (policy rate → borrowing/saving → AD → inflation; asset prices & expectations channels); quantitative easing; rules vs discretion; time lags; liquidity trap (Keynes) & the zero lower bound.
  • Supply-side policies: market-based (deregulation, privatisation, tax cuts, reducing union power, education/training) vs interventionist (industrial policy, infrastructure, R&D grants); evaluation: time lags, cost, conflicts (inflation vs growth vs BOP), effectiveness depends on the cause of the problem.
  • Policy conflicts & the policy mix; the 'impossible trinity' (fixed FX + free capital + independent monetary policy — pick two).
  • International & development: comparative advantage & the gains from trade (opportunity cost ratios), terms of trade; free trade vs protection (tariff diagrams, quota, subsidies, VERs; infant industry, strategic, dumping, health/environment arguments; WTO rounds, trading blocs — trade creation vs diversion; globalisation drivers & critics).
  • Development economics: growth vs development (GDP vs HDI vs multidimensional poverty); population & development (demographic transition, dependency ratios, the demographic dividend); barriers (debt, primary product dependence — Prebisch–Singer declining terms of trade, poor infrastructure, institutions); strategies (import substitution vs export orientation, FDI, aid — types & effectiveness debate, microfinance, fair trade, tourism); role of IMF/World Bank/WTO; sustainable development goals.

• Essay engine (8/12/20 marks): define key terms → analysis with a fully labelled diagram (axes, curves, equilibria, shifts, shaded areas) → chain of reasoning (because/therefore) → evaluation (depends on: elasticity, time period, magnitude, economy's state) → committed conclusion.
  • Data response: USE the extract data — quote numbers ('exports fell 14% in Q2'); never merely restate.
  • 12-mark structure suggestion: intro + 3 analysis paragraphs + 2 evaluation points + conclusion ≈ 2 pages.
  • P4's 20-marker is 1/3 of the paper — practise two full 20-mark essays weekly under 30 minutes each.
  • MCQs: definitions & calculation drills (elasticity, multiplier, % changes) — speed wins P1 & P3.

alevel/psy9990.b:
• The 12 core studies (know aim, method, results, conclusion, TWO criticisms each): Milgram (obedience 65% to 450V — agentic state, authority legitimacy, proximity variations) · Bandura (Bobo doll — social learning, 88% imitation) · Andrade (doodling aids concentration) · Baron-Cohen (eyes test, adults with AS/HFA — theory of mind) · Dement & Kleitman (REM & dream recall — objective measurement) · Hölzel (8-week mindfulness → grey-matter changes — neuroplasticity) · Piliavin (subway helping — diffusion of responsibility, model effect) · Saavedra & Silverman (button phobia — clinical single-case method) · Fagen (elephant operant conditioning) · Pozzulo (child line-up accuracy — own-age bias?) · Hassett (vervet monkey toy preferences — biology vs socialisation) · Perry (intranasal oxytocin & trust games).
  • Approaches: learning (behaviourism, social learning — Bandura's modelling with mediating cognitive factors), cognitive (computer analogy, schema), biological (genetics, neurochemistry, evolution), psychodynamic (Freud — repression, the unconscious; evaluation), humanistic (Maslow, Rogers — free will, self-actualisation).
  • Issues & debates: nature/nurture, reductionism vs holism, determinism vs free will, individual vs situational explanations, ethics (Milgram's legacy → modern codes), usefulness, validity (internal/external/ecological/population), reliability (test–retest, inter-rater), generalisability, the quant vs qual tension, social sensitivity.

• Experimental designs: independent groups (no order effects; participant variables), repeated measures (fewer participants; order effects → counterbalancing), matched pairs (controls both; costly matching). Lab/field/natural/quasi — control vs ecological validity trade-off.
  • Observations: covert vs overt, participant vs non-participant, structured (behavioural categories, event/time sampling) vs unstructured; inter-rater reliability checks.
  • Self-reports: questionnaires (open/closed, Likert scales, postal/online — sampling bias toward volunteers) & interviews (structured/semi/unstructured; social desirability, interviewer bias, leading questions).
  • Case studies: rich idiographic data, longitudinal, rare conditions; generalisability & retrospective bias limits.
  • Correlations: co-variables, direction/strength from scattergrams (±0.7 strong etc.), NEVER causation; multiple correlations confounding.
  • Sampling: random, systematic, stratified, opportunity, volunteer — match method to aim; sample size vs representativeness debates.
  • Hypotheses: null vs experimental/alternative, directional vs non-directional (two-tailed default unless strong prior theory); variables: IV/DV operationalised; extraneous vs confounding.
  • Analysis: descriptive (mean/median/mode; range/SD — SD as average deviation) & inferential — choosing the test: chi-squared (nominal, frequency), Spearman (correlation, ordinal), Mann-Whitney (unrelated difference, ordinal+), Wilcoxon (related difference, ordinal+); significance at p ≤ 0.05 (Type I/II errors: 0.01 cuts Type I, raises Type II); observed vs critical values & the rejection rule (remember Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon/Spearman direction rules!).
  • Ethics: BPS code — consent, deception, right to withdraw, debrief, confidentiality, protection from harm; cost–benefit reasoning & how famous studies violated each (Milgram: deception & harm; Zimbardo: withdrawal rights).

• Abnormal psychology: definitions of abnormality (statistical infrequency, deviation from social norms, failure to function, DSM/ICD classification — reliability & validity debates, cultural bias Rosenhan); schizophrenia & depression: biological explanations (genetics twin/concordance, dopamine hypothesis, neuroanatomy) vs psychological (family dysfunction, cognitive distortions Beck, learned helplessness Seligman); treatments: antipsychotics & antidepressants (SSRI mechanism, evaluation) vs CBT & family therapy; effectiveness & side-effect comparisons; the medical model critique (Szasz — 'myth of mental illness').
  • Health psychology: adherence to medical advice (factors: complexity, side effects, beliefs — Health Belief Model: perceived susceptibility, seriousness, benefits, barriers + self-efficacy; improving adherence: simplifying regimes, reminders, patient education, practitioner communication); pain (gate control theory — psychological modulation; measuring pain; chronic pain management CBT & biofeedback); stress & illness (Selye's GAS: alarm–resistance–exhaustion; immune suppression link; Type A & heart disease Friedman & Rosenman); practitioner–patient communication (doctor-centred vs patient-centred; compliance outcomes).

• Sport & exercise: motivation (intrinsic vs extrinsic, achievement goal theory, self-efficacy Bandura's four sources), arousal & performance (inverted-U; catastrophe model nods), anxiety (state vs trait; pre-competition routines), teamwork & cohesion (Steiner's model — actual productivity = potential − faulty processes), leadership styles in coaching, home advantage explanations.
  • Work & organisational: groups at work (formation stages Tuckman: forming–storming–norming–performing; groupthink Janis; social loafing Ringelmann), leadership (Fiedler contingency, transactional vs transformational applied to workplace), job satisfaction & measurement, organisational culture & change.
  • Child psychology (option): prenatal development, attachment (Bowlby, Ainsworth's strange situation, deprivation vs privation — Romanian adoptees), deprivation's long-term effects, day care debates.
  • Cognitive (option): memory models (multi-store, working memory), reconstructive memory (Loftus & Palmer's 'smashed' study — leading questions), eyewitness testimony reform.
  • Law (option): eyewitness factors (estimator vs system variables Wells), lineup procedures (sequential vs simultaneous), jury decision-making, offender profiling.
  • Environment & consumer (options): noise/crowding effects, conservation behaviour, advertising persuasion.

• P1: Section A — study-specific questions (result? conclusion? one criticism?); Section B — essay ('Discuss the contribution of the learning approach…') → describe two studies + evaluate strengths/limits + compare with another approach.
  • P2: scenario methods questions — identify the design, name the sampling, spot the confounding variable, justify a statistical test (name + why: level of measurement, related/unrelated, difference/correlation), redesign improvements; PLUS a 10-mark 'plan an investigation' with aim, hypotheses, design, sample, procedure, controls, ethics, analysis plan.
  • P3/P4 options: theory questions need named theories + studies + evaluation; application questions mirror the scenario; plan questions mirror P2's design format.
  • Evaluation toolkit phrases: 'low ecological validity because…', 'demand characteristics as participants may have guessed…', 'social desirability may have inflated…', 'the sample of 20 American undergraduates limits generalisability to…', 'reliability is supported by inter-rater agreement of 0.9'.
  • Memorise the decision tree for tests: nominal? → chi-squared · correlation? → Spearman · related difference? → Wilcoxon · unrelated difference? → Mann-Whitney.

alevel/eng9093.b:
• Levels framework: LEXIS (word choice, semantic fields, connotation, register, archaisms, neologisms, dialect/accent marking) · GRAMMAR (syntax length & complexity, sentence moods declarative/interrogative/imperative/exclamative, modality — modal verbs & hedging, pronoun choices I/we/you = stance & solidarity, active vs passive, transitivity) · FIGURES (metaphor, simile, personification, hyperbole, irony, allusion) · PHONOLOGY (alliteration, assonance, sibilance, rhythm, rhyme, onomatopoeia — in speech also pitch, stress, pace, pause, volume) · DISCOURSE (structure: headline→orientation→complication; cohesion devices: anaphora, conjunctions, lexical chains; Grice's maxims & implicature; speech acts; politeness theory Brown & Levinson; turn-taking, adjacency pairs, overlaps, interruptions, hedging in speech).
  • Commentary method: select 3–4 significant features per text, quote precisely, analyse effect, link to AUDIENCE & PURPOSE & CONTEXT; COMPARE across the pair (structure by feature or by text — keep the comparison live: 'whereas Text A…, Text B…').
  • Genre & mode: spoken vs written continua (spontaneity markers: fillers, false starts, contractions, ellipsis, non-fluency); multimodality (images, layout, font — adverts, posters).

• Directed writing: transform stimulus text(s) into a new genre/register for a new audience — the brief's audience/purpose/format marks are checklist items; plan the stance (support/oppose/nuance) and sustain it.
  • Composition: discursive/argumentative (thesis → arguments → counter-argument → verdict) & descriptive/narrative (same craft as O Level upgraded: controlled symbolism, narrative voice, structural arcs).
  • Style commentary upgrade: comment on your OWN rhetorical choices (why the tricolon? why the switch to second person?) — this meta-awareness is the A-level separator.

• World Englishes: Kachru's three circles (inner: UK/US/Aus/NZ/Canada · outer: India, Nigeria, Singapore, Pakistan — institutionalised second-language Englishes · expanding: China, Japan, Egypt — EFL). Features of outer-circle varieties (Indian English: 'prepone', reduplication 'small-small'; Nigerian English; Singapore's 'lah'; African American Vernacular features); codification debates (dictionaries of world Englishes), standard language ideology & prestige; English as a Lingua Franca (ELF) — Jenkins' core (pronunciation features needed for intelligibility: consonant sounds, vowel length, nuclear stress) — challenges native-speaker norms; ownership of English (Widdowson: 'the language has become the common property of its users').
  • Child language acquisition: pre-linguistic stages (crying → cooing → babbling 6 months → proto-words); phonological development (substitution, cluster reduction, fronting, deletion — learn the technical terms with examples); lexical development (overextension 'doggie' for all animals; underextension); grammatical development (holophrases → two-word stage ~18 months → telegraphic speech → morpheme acquisition order Brown's 14 morphemes: '-ing', plural, past irregular, possessive, articles…; overgeneralisation 'goed', 'mouses', 'sheeps'); pragmatic development (turn-taking routines, politeness); theories: behaviourist (Skinner — imitation & reinforcement; limits: novelty & overgeneralisation can't be imitated), innatist (Chomsky — LAD & universal grammar; poverty of the stimulus; the logical problem), interactionist (Bruner — LASS: scaffolding, CDS/child-directed speech features: higher pitch, repetition, simplified grammar, expansion; Vygotsky's ZPD), cognitive (Piaget — language needs cognitive readiness).
  • Evidence evaluation: CDS correlational not causal; overgeneralisation evidence for rule-learning; twin studies & 'wolf children' (Genie — critical period hypothesis Lenneberg: lateralisation by puberty).

• P1 (Reading): comprehension with own-words discipline + a summary + language analysis — same craft as 0500 deepened; timing ~2 h 15 for 50 marks.
  • P2 (Writing): directed + composition; register precision and rhetorical control are the band differentiators.
  • P3 (Language Analysis): unseen pair — 15 minutes reading & annotating before writing; organise by feature clusters; every paragraph ends with effect-on-reader-in-context.
  • P4 (Topics): knowledge questions (theories with names & dates/studies) + applied analysis of data (transcript conventions: (.), (1), CAPS for emphasis; interpret don't transcribe). Learn 4–5 transcript excerpts as practice.
  • Quote briefly & precisely; terminology deployed accurately scores higher than feature-spotting volume.
